195.s:
vyāsa uvāca
jarāsaṃdhasute kaṃsa upayeme mahābalaḥ
astiḥ prāptiś ca bho viprās tayor bhartṛhaṇaṃ harim //
195.d:
व्यास उवाच
जरासंधसुते कंस उपयेमे महाबलः
अस्तिः प्राप्तिश् च भो विप्रास् तयोर् भर्तृहणं हरिम् ॥
195.m: Vyāsa said: / The mighty Kaṃsa had married the two daughters of Jarāsaṃdha, / Asti and Prāpti, O brahmins; [against] Hari, the slayer of their husband,

195.s:
mahābalaparīvāro māgadhādhipatir balī
hantum abhyāyayau kopāj jarāsaṃdhaḥ sayādavam //
195.d:
महाबलपरीवारो मागधाधिपतिर् बली
हन्तुम् अभ्याययौ कोपाज् जरासंधः सयादवम् ॥
195.m: the mighty ruler of Magadha, Jarāsaṃdha, surrounded by a huge army, / advanced in fury to slay him along with the Yādavas.

195.s:
upetya mathurāṃ so 'tha rurodha magadheśvaraḥ
akṣauhiṇībhiḥ sainyasya trayoviṃśatibhir vṛtaḥ //
195.d:
उपेत्य मथुरां सो ऽथ रुरोध मगधेश्वरः
अक्षौहिणीभिः सैन्यस्य त्रयोविंशतिभिर् वृतः ॥
195.m: Approaching Mathurā, the ruler of Magadha then laid siege to it, / surrounded by twenty-three akṣauhiṇī divisions of troops.

195.s:
niṣkramyālpaparīvārāv ubhau rāmajanārdanau
yuyudhāte samaṃ tasya balinau balisainikaiḥ //
195.d:
निष्क्रम्याल्पपरीवाराव् उभौ रामजनार्दनौ
युयुधाते समं तस्य बलिनौ बलिसैनिकैः ॥
195.m: Going forth with a small retinue, both the mighty Rāma and Janārdana / fought equally against his mighty soldiers.

195.s:
tato balaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca matiṃ cakre mahābalaḥ
āyudhānāṃ purāṇānām ādāne munisattamāḥ //
195.d:
ततो बलश् च कृष्णश् च मतिं चक्रे महाबलः
आयुधानां पुराणानाम् आदाने मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
195.m: Then the mighty Bala and Kṛṣṇa set their minds, / O best of sages, on seizing their ancient weapons.

195.s:
anantaraṃ cakraśārṅge tūṇau cāpy akṣayau śaraiḥ
ākāśād āgatau vīrau tadā kaumodakī gadā //
195.d:
अनन्तरं चक्रशार्ङ्गे तूणौ चाप्य् अक्षयौ शरैः
आकाशाद् आगतौ वीरौ तदा कौमोदकी गदा ॥
195.m: Immediately, the discus and the Śārṅga bow, two quivers inexhaustible with arrows, / and then the Kaumodakī club came from the sky to the two heroes.

195.s:
halaṃ ca balabhadrasya gaganād āgamat karam
balasyābhimataṃ viprāḥ sunandaṃ muśalaṃ tathā //
195.d:
हलं च बलभद्रस्य गगनाद् आगमत् करम्
बलस्याभिमतं विप्राः सुनन्दं मुशलं तथा ॥
195.m: And the plow came from the sky into Balabhadra's hand, / as well as the pestle Sunanda, dear to Bala, O twice-born.

195.s:
tato yuddhe parājitya svasainyaṃ magadhādhipam
purīṃ viviśatur vīrāv ubhau rāmajanārdanau //
195.d:
ततो युद्धे पराजित्य स्वसैन्यं मगधाधिपम्
पुरीं विविशतुर् वीराव् उभौ रामजनार्दनौ ॥
195.m: Then, having defeated the ruler of Magadha and his army in battle, / both heroic brothers, Rāma and Janārdana, entered the city.

195.s:
jite tasmin sudurvṛtte jarāsaṃdhe dvijottamāḥ
jīvamāne gate tatra kṛṣṇo mene na taṃ jitam //
195.d:
जिते तस्मिन् सुदुर्वृत्ते जरासंधे द्विजोत्तमाः
जीवमाने गते तत्र कृष्णो मेने न तं जितम् ॥
195.m: When that wicked Jarāsaṃdha was defeated, O best of the twice-born, / and departed alive from there, Kṛṣṇa did not consider him truly defeated.

195.s:
punar apy ājagāmātha jarāsaṃdho balānvitaḥ
jitaś ca rāmakṛṣṇābhyām apakṛtya dvijottamāḥ //
195.d:
पुनर् अप्य् आजगामाथ जरासंधो बलान्वितः
जितश् च रामकृष्णाभ्याम् अपकृत्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
195.m: Jarāsaṃdha then returned again, accompanied by his army, / and was defeated by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, having retreated, O best of the twice-born.

195.s:
daśa cāṣṭau ca saṃgrāmān evam atyantadurmadaḥ
yadubhir māgadho rājā cakre kṛṣṇapurogamaiḥ //
195.d:
दश चाष्टौ च संग्रामान् एवम् अत्यन्तदुर्मदः
यदुभिर् मागधो राजा चक्रे कृष्णपुरोगमैः ॥
195.m: In this way, eighteen battles were fought by that exceedingly arrogant / king of Magadha with the Yadus, who were led by Kṛṣṇa.

195.s:
sarveṣv eva ca yuddheṣu yadubhiḥ sa parājitaḥ
apakrānto jarāsaṃdhaḥ svalpasainyair balādhikaḥ //
195.d:
सर्वेष्व् एव च युद्धेषु यदुभिः स पराजितः
अपक्रान्तो जरासंधः स्वल्पसैन्यैर् बलाधिकः ॥
195.m: And in all the battles he was defeated by the Yadus; / having superior forces, Jarāsaṃdha was repelled by smaller armies.

195.s:
tad balaṃ yādavānāṃ vai rakṣitaṃ yad anekaśaḥ
tat tu saṃnidhimāhātmyaṃ viṣṇor aṃśasya cakriṇaḥ //
195.d:
तद् बलं यादवानां वै रक्षितं यद् अनेकशः
तत् तु संनिधिमाहात्म्यं विष्णोर् अंशस्य चक्रिणः ॥
195.m: That army of the Yādavas was indeed protected many times: / that was the greatness of the presence of the portion of Viṣṇu, the wielder of the discus.

195.s:
manuṣyadharmaśīlasya līlā sā jagataḥ pateḥ
astrāṇy anekarūpāṇi yad arātiṣu muñcati //
195.d:
मनुष्यधर्मशीलस्य लीला सा जगतः पतेः
अस्त्राण्य् अनेकरूपाणि यद् अरातिषु मुञ्चति ॥
195.m: It is the sport of the Lord of the world acting according to human nature, / that he releases weapons of diverse forms against enemies.

195.s:
manasaiva jagatsṛṣṭisaṃhāraṃ tu karoti yaḥ
tasyāripakṣakṣapaṇe kiyān udyamavistaraḥ //
195.d:
मनसैव जगत्सृष्टिसंहारं तु करोति यः
तस्यारिपक्षक्षपणे कियान् उद्यमविस्तरः ॥
195.m: For one who performs the creation and destruction of the universe by mere thought, / what great effort is there in destroying the host of enemies?

195.s:
tathāpi ca manuṣyāṇāṃ dharmas tadanuvartanam
kurvan balavatā saṃdhiṃ hīnair yuddhaṃ karoty asau //
195.d:
तथापि च मनुष्याणां धर्मस् तदनुवर्तनम्
कुर्वन् बलवता संधिं हीनैर् युद्धं करोत्य् असौ ॥
195.m: Even so, following the dharma of human beings, / he makes an alliance with the strong and fights with the inferior.

195.s:
sāma copapradānaṃ ca tathā bhedaṃ ca darśayan
karoti daṇḍapātaṃ ca kvacid eva palāyanam //
195.d:
साम चोपप्रदानं च तथा भेदं च दर्शयन्
करोति दण्डपातं च क्वचिद् एव पलायनम् ॥
195.m: Employing conciliation, bribery, and also division, / he uses punishment, and occasionally takes flight.

195.s:
manuṣyadehināṃ ceṣṭām ity evam anuvartate
līlā jagatpates tasya cchandataḥ saṃpravartate //
195.d:
मनुष्यदेहिनां चेष्टाम् इत्य् एवम् अनुवर्तते
लीला जगत्पतेस् तस्य च्छन्दतः संप्रवर्तते ॥
195.m: In this way he imitates the conduct of embodied humans; / the sport of that Lord of the universe proceeds according to his will.

196.s:
vyāsa uvāca
gārgyaṃ goṣṭhe dvijo śyālaḥ ṣaṇḍha ity uktavān dvijāḥ
yadūnāṃ saṃnidhau sarve jahasur yādavās tadā //
196.d:
व्यास उवाच
गार्ग्यं गोष्ठे द्विजो श्यालः षण्ढ इत्य् उक्तवान् द्विजाः
यदूनां संनिधौ सर्वे जहसुर् यादवास् तदा ॥
196.m: Vyāsa said: / In the cow-pen, a twice-born brother-in-law said to Gārgya, 'You eunuch!', O twice-born; / then in the presence of the Yadus, all the Yādavas laughed.

196.s:
tataḥ kopasamāviṣṭo dakṣiṇāpatham etya saḥ
sutam icchaṃs tapas tepe yaducakrabhayāvaham //
196.d:
ततः कोपसमाविष्टो दक्षिणापथम् एत्य सः
सुतम् इच्छंस् तपस् तेपे यदुचक्रभयावहम् ॥
196.m: Then, overcome with rage, he went to the southern region; / desiring a son who would terrify the Yadu host, he performed austerities.

196.s:
ārādhayan mahādevaṃ so 'yaś cūrṇam abhakṣayat
dadau varaṃ ca tuṣṭo 'sau varṣe dvādaśake haraḥ //
196.d:
आराधयन् महादेवं सो ऽयश् चूर्णम् अभक्षयत्
ददौ वरं च तुष्टो ऽसौ वर्षे द्वादशके हरः ॥
196.m: Worshiping Mahādeva, he ate iron powder; / and pleased after twelve years, Hara granted him a boon.

196.s:
saṃbhāvayām āsa sa taṃ yavaneśo hy anātmajam
tadyoṣitsaṃgamāc cāsya putro 'bhūd alisaprabhaḥ //
196.d:
संभावयाम् आस स तं यवनेशो ह्य् अनात्मजम्
तद्योषित्संगमाच् चास्य पुत्रो ऽभूद् अलिसप्रभः ॥
196.m: The childless king of the Yavanas honored him; / and through union with his wife, a son was born to him, lustrous like a black bee.

196.s:
taṃ kālayavanaṃ nāma rājye sve yavaneśvaraḥ
abhiṣicya vanaṃ yāto vajrāgrakaṭhinorasam //
196.d:
तं कालयवनं नाम राज्ये स्वे यवनेश्वरः
अभिषिच्य वनं यातो वज्राग्रकठिनोरसम् ॥
196.m: Having consecrated him, named Kālayavana, whose chest was as hard as the tip of a thunderbolt, / in his own kingdom, the lord of the Yavanas departed to the forest.

196.s:
sa tu vīryamadonmattaḥ pṛthivyāṃ balino nṛpān
papraccha nāradaś cāsmai kathayām āsa yādavān //
196.d:
स तु वीर्यमदोन्मत्तः पृथिव्यां बलिनो नृपान्
पप्रच्छ नारदश् चास्मै कथयाम् आस यादवान् ॥
196.m: Intoxicated by the pride of his prowess, he asked / about the powerful kings on earth, and Nārada told him of the Yādavas.

196.s:
mlecchakoṭisahasrāṇāṃ sahasraiḥ so 'pi saṃvṛtaḥ
gajāśvarathasaṃpannaiś cakāra paramodyamam //
196.d:
म्लेच्छकोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रैः सो ऽपि संवृतः
गजाश्वरथसंपन्नैश् चकार परमोद्यमम् ॥
196.m: Surrounded by thousands of millions of Mlecchas, / equipped with elephants, horses, and chariots, he made a great exertion.

196.s:
prayayau cātavacchinnaiḥ prayāṇaiḥ sa dine dine
yādavān prati sāmarṣo munayo mathurāṃ purīm //
196.d:
प्रययौ चातवच्छिन्नैः प्रयाणैः स दिने दिने
यादवान् प्रति सामर्षो मुनयो मथुरां पुरीम् ॥
196.m: With uninterrupted daily marches, he advanced / toward the Yādavas in anger, O sages, toward the city of Mathurā.

196.s:
kṛṣṇo 'pi cintayām āsa kṣapitaṃ yādavaṃ balam
yavanena samālokya māgadhaḥ saṃprayāsyati //
196.d:
कृष्णो ऽपि चिन्तयाम् आस क्षपितं यादवं बलम्
यवनेन समालोक्य मागधः संप्रयास्यति ॥
196.m: Kṛṣṇa too considered: 'Seeing the Yādava force destroyed / by the Yavana, the ruler of Magadha will advance.

196.s:
māgadhasya balaṃ kṣīṇaṃ sa kālayavano balī
hantā tad idam āyātaṃ yadūnāṃ vyasanaṃ dvidhā //
196.d:
मागधस्य बलं क्षीणं स कालयवनो बली
हन्ता तद् इदम् आयातं यदूनां व्यसनं द्विधा ॥
196.m: The force of the ruler of Magadha is diminished, while that Kālayavana is strong; / alas, this misfortune has come upon the Yadus from two sides!

196.s:
tasmād durgaṃ kariṣyāmi yadūnām atidurjayam
striyo 'pi yatra yudhyeyuḥ kiṃ punar vṛṣṇiyādavāḥ //
196.d:
तस्माद् दुर्गं करिष्यामि यदूनाम् अतिदुर्जयम्
स्त्रियो ऽपि यत्र युध्येयुः किं पुनर् वृष्णियादवाः ॥
196.m: Therefore, I shall build an invincible fortress for the Yadus, / where even women could fight, not to mention the Vṛṣṇis and Yādavas.

196.s:
mayi matte pramatte vā supte pravasite 'pi vā
yādavābhibhavaṃ duṣṭā mā kurvan vairiṇo 'dhikam //
196.d:
मयि मत्ते प्रमत्ते वा सुप्ते प्रवसिते ऽपि वा
यादवाभिभवं दुष्टा मा कुर्वन् वैरिणो ऽधिकम् ॥
196.m: Whether I am intoxicated, heedless, asleep, or abroad, / the wicked enemies must not greatly overpower the Yādavas.'

196.s:
iti saṃcintya govindo yojanāni mahodadhim
yayāce dvādaśa purīṃ dvārakāṃ tatra nirmame //
196.d:
इति संचिन्त्य गोविन्दो योजनानि महोदधिम्
ययाचे द्वादश पुरीं द्वारकां तत्र निर्ममे ॥
196.m: Thinking thus, Govinda requested twelve yojanas / from the great ocean, and there he constructed the city of Dvārakā,

196.s:
mahodyānāṃ mahāvaprāṃ taḍāgaśataśobhitām
prākāraśatasaṃbādhām indrasyevāmarāvatīm //
196.d:
महोद्यानां महावप्रां तडागशतशोभिताम्
प्राकारशतसंबाधाम् इन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम् ॥
196.m: with great gardens, massive ramparts, adorned with hundreds of ponds, / crowded with hundreds of walls, like Indra's Amarāvatī.

196.s:
mathurāvāsinaṃ lokaṃ tatrānīya janārdanaḥ
āsanne kālayavane mathurāṃ ca svayaṃ yayau //
196.d:
मथुरावासिनं लोकं तत्रानीय जनार्दनः
आसन्ने कालयवने मथुरां च स्वयं ययौ ॥
196.m: Bringing the people living in Mathurā there, / Janārdana himself went to Mathurā as Kālayavana drew near.

196.s:
bahir āvāsite sainye mathurāyā nirāyudhaḥ
nirjagāma sa govindo dadarśa yavanaś ca tam //
196.d:
बहिर् आवासिते सैन्ये मथुराया निरायुधः
निर्जगाम स गोविन्दो ददर्श यवनश् च तम् ॥
196.m: While the army was encamped outside Mathurā, unarmed / Govinda came out, and the Yavana saw him.

196.s:
sa jñātvā vāsudevaṃ taṃ bāhupraharaṇo nṛpaḥ
anuyāto mahāyogicetobhiḥ prāpyate na yaḥ //
196.d:
स ज्ञात्वा वासुदेवं तं बाहुप्रहरणो नृपः
अनुयातो महायोगिचेतोभिः प्राप्यते न यः ॥
196.m: Recognizing him as Vāsudeva, that king, armed only with his bare arms, / pursued him who cannot be attained even by the minds of great yogins.

196.s:
tenānuyātaḥ kṛṣṇo 'pi praviveśa mahāguhām
yatra śete mahāvīryo mucukundo nareśvaraḥ //
196.d:
तेनानुयातः कृष्णो ऽपि प्रविवेश महागुहाम्
यत्र शेते महावीर्यो मुचुकुन्दो नरेश्वरः ॥
196.m: Pursued by him, Kṛṣṇa entered a great cave, / where the greatly heroic king Mucukunda lay asleep.

196.s:
so 'pi praviṣṭo yavano dṛṣṭvā śayyāgataṃ naram
pādena tāḍayām āsa kṛṣṇaṃ matvā sa durmatiḥ //
196.d:
सो ऽपि प्रविष्टो यवनो दृष्ट्वा शय्यागतं नरम्
पादेन ताडयाम् आस कृष्णं मत्वा स दुर्मतिः ॥
196.m: Having also entered, the Yavana saw a man lying on a bed; / mistaking him for Kṛṣṇa, the fool struck him with his foot.

196.s:
dṛṣṭamātraś ca tenāsau jajvāla yavano 'gninā
tatkrodhajena munayo bhasmībhūtaś ca tatkṣaṇāt //
196.d:
दृष्टमात्रश् च तेनासौ जज्वाल यवनो ऽग्निना
तत्क्रोधजेन मुनयो भस्मीभूतश् च तत्क्षणात् ॥
196.m: No sooner was he looked upon by him than the Yavana blazed with fire / born of his wrath, O sages, and in that instant was reduced to ashes.

196.s:
sa hi devāsure yuddhe gatvā jitvā mahāsurān
nidrārtaḥ sumahākālaṃ nidrāṃ vavre varaṃ surān //
196.d:
स हि देवासुरे युद्धे गत्वा जित्वा महासुरान्
निद्रार्तः सुमहाकालं निद्रां वव्रे वरं सुरान् ॥
196.m: For having gone to the battle between gods and asuras and conquered the great asuras, / overcome with fatigue, he chose long sleep as a boon from the gods.

196.s:
proktaś ca devaiḥ saṃsuptaṃ yas tvām utthāpayiṣyati
dehajenāgninā sadyaḥ sa tu bhasmībhaviṣyati //
196.d:
प्रोक्तश् च देवैः संसुप्तं यस् त्वाम् उत्थापयिष्यति
देहजेनाग्निना सद्यः स तु भस्मीभविष्यति ॥
196.m: And he was told by the gods: 'Whoever awakens you while you are asleep / shall instantly be reduced to ashes by the fire born of your body.'

196.s:
evaṃ dagdhvā sa taṃ pāpaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca madhusūdanam
kas tvam ity āha so 'py āha jāto 'haṃ śaśinaḥ kule //
196.d:
एवं दग्ध्वा स तं पापं दृष्ट्वा च मधुसूदनम्
कस् त्वम् इत्य् आह सो ऽप्य् आह जातो ऽहं शशिनः कुले ॥
196.m: Having thus burned that wicked one and seen Madhusūdana, / he said, 'Who are you?' He replied, 'I was born in the lineage of the Moon,

196.s:
vasudevasya tanayo yaduvaṃśasamudbhavaḥ
mucukundo 'pi tac chrutvā vṛddhagārgyavacaḥ smaran //
196.d:
वसुदेवस्य तनयो यदुवंशसमुद्भवः
मुचुकुन्दो ऽपि तच् छ्रुत्वा वृद्धगार्ग्यवचः स्मरन् ॥
196.m: the son of Vasudeva, born in the Yadu dynasty.' / Mucukunda, hearing this and recalling the words of the elder Gārgya,

196.s:
saṃsmṛtya praṇipatyainaṃ sarvaṃ sarveśvaraṃ harim
prāha jñāto bhavān viṣṇor aṃśas tvaṃ parameśvaraḥ //
196.d:
संस्मृत्य प्रणिपत्यैनं सर्वं सर्वेश्वरं हरिम्
प्राह ज्ञातो भवान् विष्णोर् अंशस् त्वं परमेश्वरः ॥
196.m: recollecting and bowing to him, Hari, the all-pervading Lord of all, / said: 'I know you: you are a portion of Viṣṇu, the supreme Lord.

196.s:
purā gārgyeṇa kathitam aṣṭāviṃśatime yuge
dvāparānte harer janma yaduvaṃśe bhaviṣyati //
196.d:
पुरा गार्ग्येण कथितम् अष्टाविंशतिमे युगे
द्वापरान्ते हरेर् जन्म यदुवंशे भविष्यति ॥
196.m: Formerly it was told by Gārgya that in the twenty-eighth age, / at the end of Dvāpara, Hari's birth will take place in the Yadu dynasty.'

196.s:
sa tvaṃ prāpto na saṃdeho martyānām upakārakṛt
tathā hi sumahat tejo nālaṃ soḍhum ahaṃ tava //
196.d:
स त्वं प्राप्तो न संदेहो मर्त्यानाम् उपकारकृत्
तथा हि सुमहत् तेजो नालं सोढुम् अहं तव ॥
196.m: It is you who have arrived, of that there is no doubt, to bring aid to mortals; / for indeed, I am not able to endure your tremendous splendor.

196.s:
tathā hi sumahāmbhodadhvanidhīrataraṃ tataḥ
vākyaṃ tam iti hovāca yuṣmatpādasulālitam //
196.d:
तथा हि सुमहाम्भोदध्वनिधीरतरं ततः
वाक्यं तम् इति होवाच युष्मत्पादसुलालितम् ॥
196.m: And then he spoke this speech to him, grave as the roar of the mighty ocean, / pampered by your feet:

196.s:
devāsure mahāyuddhe daityāś ca sumahābhaṭāḥ
na śekus te mahat tejas tat tejo na sahāmy aham //
196.d:
देवासुरे महायुद्धे दैत्याश् च सुमहाभटाः
न शेकुस् ते महत् तेजस् तत् तेजो न सहाम्य् अहम् ॥
196.m: 'In the great battle between the gods and the asuras, the daityas, though mighty warriors, / could not endure your great splendor; that splendor of yours I cannot bear.

196.s:
saṃsārapatitasyaiko jantos tvaṃ śaraṇaṃ param
saṃprasīda prapannārtihartā hara mamāśubham //
196.d:
संसारपतितस्यैको जन्तोस् त्वं शरणं परम्
संप्रसीद प्रपन्नार्तिहर्ता हर ममाशुभम् ॥
196.m: You are the sole supreme refuge of a creature fallen into saṃsāra. / Be gracious, O remover of the distress of those who take refuge; remove my misfortune!

196.s:
tvaṃ payonidhayaḥ śailāḥ saritaś ca vanāni ca
medinī gaganaṃ vāyur āpo 'gnis tvaṃ tathā pumān //
196.d:
त्वं पयोनिधयः शैलाः सरितश् च वनानि च
मेदिनी गगनं वायुर् आपो ऽग्निस् त्वं तथा पुमान् ॥
196.m: You are the oceans, the mountains, the rivers, and the forests; / you are the earth, the sky, the wind, the waters, the fire, and you are the spirit (pumān).

196.s:
puṃsaḥ parataraṃ sarvaṃ vyāpya janma vikalpavat
śabdādihīnam ajaraṃ vṛddhikṣayavivarjitam //
196.d:
पुंसः परतरं सर्वं व्याप्य जन्म विकल्पवत्
शब्दादिहीनम् अजरं वृद्धिक्षयविवर्जितम् ॥
196.m: Higher than the spirit, pervading all, is that which is subject to modification like ordinary birth, / free of sound and the other [sense objects], ageless, devoid of increase and decay.

196.s:
tvatto 'marās tu pitaro yakṣagandharvarākṣasāḥ
siddhāś cāpsarasas tvatto manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ khagāḥ //
196.d:
त्वत्तो ऽमरास् तु पितरो यक्षगन्धर्वराक्षसाः
सिद्धाश् चाप्सरसस् त्वत्तो मनुष्याः पशवः खगाः ॥
196.m: From you come the immortals, the ancestors, the yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas; / from you come the siddhas and apsarases, humans, beasts, and birds;

196.s:
sarīsṛpā mṛgāḥ sarve tvattaś caiva mahīruhāḥ
yac ca bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyad vā kiṃcid atra carācare //
196.d:
सरीसृपा मृगाः सर्वे त्वत्तश् चैव महीरुहाः
यच् च भूतं भविष्यद् वा किंचिद् अत्र चराचरे ॥
196.m: the reptiles, all the wild beasts, and from you alone the trees, / and whatever exists or shall come to be here among moving and unmoving things.

196.s:
amūrtaṃ mūrtam athavā sthūlaṃ sūkṣmataraṃ tathā
tat sarvaṃ tvaṃ jagatkartar nāsti kiṃcit tvayā vinā //
196.d:
अमूर्तं मूर्तम् अथवा स्थूलं सूक्ष्मतरं तथा
तत् सर्वं त्वं जगत्कर्तर् नास्ति किंचित् त्वया विना ॥
196.m: Whether formless or possessing form, coarse or most subtle, / you are all that, O creator of the universe; nothing exists without you.

196.s:
mayā saṃsāracakre 'smin bhramatā bhagavan sadā
tāpatrayābhibhūtena na prāptā nirvṛtiḥ kvacit //
196.d:
मया संसारचक्रे ऽस्मिन् भ्रमता भगवन् सदा
तापत्रयाभिभूतेन न प्राप्ता निर्वृतिः क्वचित् ॥
196.m: Wandering constantly in this wheel of saṃsāra, O Lord, / overcome by the three kinds of afflictions, I have nowhere found peace.

196.s:
duḥkhāny eva sukhānīti mṛgatṛṣṇājalāśayaḥ
mayā nātha gṛhītāni tāni tāpāya me 'bhavan //
196.d:
दुःखान्य् एव सुखानीति मृगतृष्णाजलाशयः
मया नाथ गृहीतानि तानि तापाय मे ऽभवन् ॥
196.m: Miseries were seized upon by me as pleasures, O Lord, like the water of a mirage, / and they turned into affliction for me.

196.s:
rājyam urvī balaṃ kośo mitrapakṣas tathātmajāḥ
bhāryā bhṛtyajanā ye ca śabdādyā viṣayāḥ prabho //
196.d:
राज्यम् उर्वी बलं कोशो मित्रपक्षस् तथात्मजाः
भार्या भृत्यजना ये च शब्दाद्या विषयाः प्रभो ॥
196.m: Kingship, the earth, an army, the treasury, allies, and sons, / wife, servants, and sense objects such as sound, O Lord—

196.s:
sukhabuddhyā mayā sarvaṃ gṛhītam idam avyaya
pariṇāme ca deveśa tāpātmakam abhūn mama //
196.d:
सुखबुद्ध्या मया सर्वं गृहीतम् इदम् अव्यय
परिणामे च देवेश तापात्मकम् अभून् मम ॥
196.m: all this was grasped by me with an idea of happiness, O imperishable one; / and in the end, O lord of the gods, it has turned into anguish for me.

196.s:
devalokagatiṃ prāpto nātha devagaṇo 'pi hi
mattaḥ sāhāyyakāmo 'bhūc chāśvatī kutra nirvṛtiḥ //
196.d:
देवलोकगतिं प्राप्तो नाथ देवगणो ऽपि हि
मत्तः साहाय्यकामो ऽभूच् छाश्वती कुत्र निर्वृतिः ॥
196.m: Though having attained to the realm of the gods, O Lord, even the host of the gods / desired assistance from me; where then is eternal peace?

196.s:
tvām anārādhya jagatāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhavāspadam
śāśvatī prāpyate kena parameśvara nirvṛtiḥ //
196.d:
त्वाम् अनाराध्य जगतां सर्वेषां प्रभवास्पदम्
शाश्वती प्राप्यते केन परमेश्वर निर्वृतिः ॥
196.m: Without worshiping you, the abode of origin of all the worlds, / by whom, O supreme lord, can eternal peace be attained?

196.s:
tvanmāyāmūḍhamanaso janmamṛtyujarādikān
avāpya pāpān paśyanti pretarājānam antarā //
196.d:
त्वन्मायामूढमनसो जन्ममृत्युजरादिकान्
अवाप्य पापान् पश्यन्ति प्रेतराजानम् अन्तरा ॥
196.m: Those whose minds are bewildered by your illusory power, having suffered birth, death, old age, and the like, / being sinful, behold the king of the dead in the hereafter.

196.s:
tataḥ pāśaśatair baddhā narakeṣv atidāruṇam
prāpnuvanti mahad duḥkhaṃ viśvarūpam idaṃ tava //
196.d:
ततः पाशशतैर् बद्धा नरकेष्व् अतिदारुणम्
प्राप्नुवन्ति महद् दुःखं विश्वरूपम् इदं तव ॥
196.m: Then, bound with hundreds of fetters, in hells they experience / exceedingly terrible, vast suffering; this is your universal form.

196.s:
aham atyantaviṣayī mohitas tava māyayā
mamatvāgādhagartānte bhramāmi parameśvara //
196.d:
अहम् अत्यन्तविषयी मोहितस् तव मायया
ममत्वागाधगर्तान्ते भ्रमामि परमेश्वर ॥
196.m: Extremely attached to sense objects, deluded by your illusory power, / I wander on the brink of the deep pit of mine-ness, O supreme lord.

196.s:
so 'haṃ tvāṃ śaraṇam apāram īśam īḍyaṃ
saṃprāptaḥ paramapadaṃ yato na kiṃcit
saṃsāraśramaparitāpataptacetā
nirviṇṇe pariṇatadhāmni sābhilāṣaḥ
196.d:
सो ऽहं त्वां शरणम् अपारम् ईशम् ईड्यं
संप्राप्तः परमपदं यतो न किंचित्
संसारश्रमपरितापतप्तचेता
निर्विण्णे परिणतधाम्नि साभिलाषः
196.m: Such as I am, I have taken refuge in you, the shoreless, praiseworthy Lord, / beyond whom there is no higher state; / my mind scorched by the exhaustion and suffering of saṃsāra, / weary of it, and longing for your perfected abode.'

197.s:
vyāsa uvāca
itthaṃ stutas tadā tena mucukundena dhīmatā
prāheśaḥ sarvabhūtānām anādinidhano hariḥ //
197.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्थं स्तुतस् तदा तेन मुचुकुन्देन धीमता
प्राहेशः सर्वभूतानाम् अनादिनिधनो हरिः ॥
197.m: Vyāsa said: / Praised in this manner then by the wise Mucukunda, / the Lord of all beings, Hari, without beginning or end, said:

197.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
yathābhivāñchitāṃl lokān divyān gaccha nareśvara
avyāhataparaiśvaryo matprasādopabṛṃhitaḥ //
197.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
यथाभिवाञ्छितांल् लोकान् दिव्यान् गच्छ नरेश्वर
अव्याहतपरैश्वर्यो मत्प्रसादोपबृंहितः ॥
197.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / 'Go to the celestial worlds as you have desired, O king of men, / your supreme sovereignty unobstructed, magnified by my grace.

197.s:
bhuktvā divyān mahābhogān bhaviṣyasi mahākule
jātismaro matprasādāt tato mokṣam avāpsyasi //
197.d:
भुक्त्वा दिव्यान् महाभोगान् भविष्यसि महाकुले
जातिस्मरो मत्प्रसादात् ततो मोक्षम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
197.m: Having enjoyed celestial, great delights, you will be born in an illustrious lineage, / recollecting your previous births through my grace; and after that you will attain liberation.'

197.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktaḥ praṇipatyeśaṃ jagatām acyutaṃ nṛpaḥ
guhāmukhād viniṣkrānto dadṛśe so 'lpakān narān //
197.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्तः प्रणिपत्येशं जगताम् अच्युतं नृपः
गुहामुखाद् विनिष्क्रान्तो ददृशे सो ऽल्पकान् नरान् ॥
197.m: Vyāsa said: / Having been addressed thus, the king bowed down to the lord of the worlds, Acyuta, / emerged from the mouth of the cave, and saw dwarfed people.

197.s:
tataḥ kaliyugaṃ jñātvā prāptaṃ taptuṃ tato nṛpaḥ
naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ prayayau gandhamādanam //
197.d:
ततः कलियुगं ज्ञात्वा प्राप्तं तप्तुं ततो नृपः
नरनारायणस्थानं प्रययौ गन्धमादनम् ॥
197.m: Then, knowing that the Kali age had arrived, the king went to the Gandhamādana mountain, / the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, to perform penance.

197.s:
kṛṣṇo 'pi ghātayitvārim upāyena hi tadbalam
jagrāha mathurām etya hastyaśvasyandanojjvalam //
197.d:
कृष्णो ऽपि घातयित्वारिम् उपायेन हि तद्बलम्
जग्राह मथुराम् एत्य हस्त्यश्वस्यन्दनोज्ज्वलम् ॥
197.m: Kṛṣṇa, having caused his enemy to be slain through a stratagem, / came to Mathurā and seized his army, resplendent with elephants, horses, and chariots.

197.s:
ānīya cograsenāya dvāravatyāṃ nyavedayat
parābhibhavaniḥśaṅkaṃ babhūva ca yadoḥ kulam //
197.d:
आनीय चोग्रसेनाय द्वारवत्यां न्यवेदयत्
पराभिभवनिःशङ्कं बभूव च यदोः कुलम् ॥
197.m: Bringing it to Dvāravatī, he presented it to Ugrasena; / and the lineage of Yadu became free from fear of humiliation by enemies.

197.s:
baladevo 'pi viprendrāḥ praśāntākhilavigrahaḥ
jñātidarśanasotkaṇṭhaḥ prayayau nandagokulam //
197.d:
बलदेवो ऽपि विप्रेन्द्राः प्रशान्ताखिलविग्रहः
ज्ञातिदर्शनसोत्कण्ठः प्रययौ नन्दगोकुलम् ॥
197.m: Baladeva too, O best of brahmins, when all hostilities had ceased, / set out for the cowherd village of Nanda, eager to see his kin.

197.s:
tato gopāś ca gopyaś ca yathāpūrvam amitrajit
tathaivābhyavadat premṇā bahumānapuraḥsaram //
197.d:
ततो गोपाश् च गोप्यश् च यथापूर्वम् अमित्रजित्
तथैवाभ्यवदत् प्रेम्णा बहुमानपुरःसरम् ॥
197.m: Then the cowherds and the gopīs, just as before, greeted that conqueror of enemies / with love and deep respect.

197.s:
kaiś cāpi saṃpariṣvaktaḥ kāṃścit sa pariṣasvaje
hāsaṃ cakre samaṃ kaiścid gopagopījanais tathā //
197.d:
कैश् चापि संपरिष्वक्तः कांश्चित् स परिषस्वजे
हासं चक्रे समं कैश्चिद् गोपगोपीजनैस् तथा ॥
197.m: He was embraced by some, and he embraced others; / he laughed together with some among the cowherds and gopīs.

197.s:
priyāṇy anekāny avadan gopās tatra halāyudham
gopyaś ca premamuditāḥ procuḥ serṣyam athāparāḥ //
197.d:
प्रियाण्य् अनेकान्य् अवदन् गोपास् तत्र हलायुधम्
गोप्यश् च प्रेममुदिताः प्रोचुः सेर्ष्यम् अथापराः ॥
197.m: The cowherds spoke many affectionate words there to Halāyudha; / and the gopīs, joyful with love, spoke, while others did so jealously.

197.s:
gopyaḥ papracchur aparā nāgarījanavallabhaḥ
kaccid āste sukhaṃ kṛṣṇaś calatpremarasākulaḥ //
197.d:
गोप्यः पप्रच्छुर् अपरा नागरीजनवल्लभः
कच्चिद् आस्ते सुखं कृष्णश् चलत्प्रेमरसाकुलः ॥
197.m: Other gopīs asked: 'Is Kṛṣṇa, beloved of the city women, / dwelling in comfort, agitated with fickle amorous longing?

197.s:
asmacceṣṭopahasanaṃ na kaccit purayoṣitām
saubhāgyamānam adhikaṃ karoti kṣaṇasauhṛdaḥ //
197.d:
अस्मच्चेष्टोपहसनं न कच्चित् पुरयोषिताम्
सौभाग्यमानम् अधिकं करोति क्षणसौहृदः ॥
197.m: Does he whose affection lasts but a moment not increase the city women's pride in their good fortune / by mocking our rustic actions?

197.s:
kaccit smarati naḥ kṛṣṇo gītānugamanaṃ kṛtam
apy asau mātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ sakṛd apy āgamiṣyati //
197.d:
कच्चित् स्मरति नः कृष्णो गीतानुगमनं कृतम्
अप्य् असौ मातरं द्रष्टुं सकृद् अप्य् आगमिष्यति ॥
197.m: Does Kṛṣṇa remember our accompanying his singing? / Will he come even once to see his mother?

197.s:
athavā kiṃ tadālāpaiḥ kriyantām aparāḥ kathāḥ
yad asmābhir vinā tena vināsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati //
197.d:
अथवा किं तदालापैः क्रियन्ताम् अपराः कथाः
यद् अस्माभिर् विना तेन विनास्माकं भविष्यति ॥
197.m: Or rather, what is the use of talks about him? Let other conversations be pursued! / What will happen without him, will happen without us.

197.s:
pitā mātā tathā bhrātā bhartā bandhujanaś ca kaḥ
na tyaktas tatkṛte śmābhir akṛtajñas tato hi saḥ //
197.d:
पिता माता तथा भ्राता भर्ता बन्धुजनश् च कः
न त्यक्तस् तत्कृते श्माभिर् अकृतज्ञस् ततो हि सः ॥
197.m: Father, mother, brother, husband, and relatives—who among them / was not abandoned by us for his sake? Therefore he is ungrateful!

197.s:
tathāpi kaccid ātmīyam ihāgamanasaṃśrayam
karoti kṛṣṇo vaktavyaṃ bhavatā vacanāmṛtam //
197.d:
तथापि कच्चिद् आत्मीयम् इहागमनसंश्रयम्
करोति कृष्णो वक्तव्यं भवता वचनामृतम् ॥
197.m: Even so, does Kṛṣṇa make any nectar-like statement of his own / regarding coming here, which you might tell us?'

197.s:
dāmodaro 'sau govindaḥ purastrīsaktamānasaḥ
apetaprītir asmāsu durdarśaḥ pratibhāti naḥ //
197.d:
दामोदरो ऽसौ गोविन्दः पुरस्त्रीसक्तमानसः
अपेतप्रीतिर् अस्मासु दुर्दर्शः प्रतिभाति नः ॥
197.m: 'That Dāmodara, Govinda, whose mind is attached to the women of the city, / has lost affection for us and seems hard for us to see.'

197.s:
vyāsa uvāca
āmantritaḥ sa kṛṣṇeti punar dāmodareti ca
jahasuḥ susvaraṃ gopyo hariṇā kṛṣṭacetasaḥ //
197.d:
व्यास उवाच
आमन्त्रितः स कृष्णेति पुनर् दामोदरेति च
जहसुः सुस्वरं गोप्यो हरिणा कृष्टचेतसः ॥
197.m: Vyāsa said: / Having addressed him as 'Kṛṣṇa' and again as 'Dāmodara,' / the gopīs, their hearts drawn by Hari, laughed melodiously.

197.s:
saṃdeśaiḥ saumyamadhuraiḥ premagarbhair agarvitaiḥ
rāmeṇāśvāsitā gopyaḥ kṛṣṇasyātimadhusvaraiḥ //
197.d:
संदेशैः सौम्यमधुरैः प्रेमगर्भैर् अगर्वितैः
रामेणाश्वासिता गोप्यः कृष्णस्यातिमधुस्वरैः ॥
197.m: With gentle and sweet messages from Kṛṣṇa, filled with love and devoid of arrogance, / in very sweet tones, the gopīs were comforted by Rāma.

197.s:
gopaiś ca pūrvavad rāmaḥ parihāsamanoharaiḥ
kathāś cakāra premṇā ca saha tair vrajabhūmiṣu //
197.d:
गोपैश् च पूर्ववद् रामः परिहासमनोहरैः
कथाश् चकार प्रेम्णा च सह तैर् व्रजभूमिषु ॥
197.m: And with the cowherds, as before, Rāma conversed with love / in charming, humorous ways in the pastures of Vraja.

198.s:
vyāsa uvāca
vane viharatas tasya saha gopair mahātmanaḥ
mānuṣacchadmarūpasya śeṣasya dharaṇībhṛtaḥ //
198.d:
व्यास उवाच
वने विहरतस् तस्य सह गोपैर् महात्मनः
मानुषच्छद्मरूपस्य शेषस्य धरणीभृतः ॥
198.m: Vyāsa said: / As the great-souled Śeṣa, supporter of the earth, disguised in human form, / was sporting in the forest with the cowherds—

198.s:
niṣpāditorukāryasya kāryeṇaivāvatāriṇaḥ
upabhogārtham atyarthaṃ varuṇaḥ prāha vāruṇīm //
198.d:
निष्पादितोरुकार्यस्य कार्येणैवावतारिणः
उपभोगार्थम् अत्यर्थं वरुणः प्राह वारुणीम् ॥
198.m: having accomplished great tasks, having descended precisely on account of his mission— / Varuṇa spoke to Vāruṇī for the sake of his exquisite enjoyment:

198.s:
varuṇa uvāca
abhīṣṭāṃ sarvadā hy asya madire tvaṃ mahaujasaḥ
anantasyopabhogāya tasya gaccha mude śubhe //
198.d:
वरुण उवाच
अभीष्टां सर्वदा ह्य् अस्य मदिरे त्वं महौजसः
अनन्तस्योपभोगाय तस्य गच्छ मुदे शुभे ॥
198.m: Varuṇa said: / 'O wine, you are ever dear to that being of great splendor; / go to that Ananta for his enjoyment and pleasure, O auspicious one!'

198.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktā vāruṇī tena saṃnidhānam athākarot
vṛndāvanataṭotpannakadambatarukoṭare //
198.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्ता वारुणी तेन संनिधानम् अथाकरोत्
वृन्दावनतटोत्पन्नकदम्बतरुकोटरे ॥
198.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus addressed by him, Vāruṇī then manifested herself / in the hollow of a kadamba tree growing on the slopes of Vṛndāvana.

198.s:
vicaran baladevo 'pi madirāgandham uddhatam
āghrāya madirāharṣam avāpātha purātanam //
198.d:
विचरन् बलदेवो ऽपि मदिरागन्धम् उद्धतम्
आघ्राय मदिराहर्षम् अवापाथ पुरातनम् ॥
198.m: While strolling, Baladeva inhaled the intoxicating aroma of wine, / and he experienced his ancient delight in wine.

198.s:
tataḥ kadambāt sahasā madyadhārāṃ sa lāṅgalī
patantīṃ vīkṣya munayaḥ prayayau paramāṃ mudam //
198.d:
ततः कदम्बात् सहसा मद्यधारां स लाङ्गली
पतन्तीं वीक्ष्य मुनयः प्रययौ परमां मुदम् ॥
198.m: Then, seeing a stream of wine suddenly flowing from the kadamba tree, / the plow-bearer, O sages, attained supreme joy.

198.s:
papau ca gopagopībhiḥ samaveto mudānvitaḥ
upagīyamāno lalitaṃ gītavādyaviśāradaiḥ //
198.d:
पपौ च गोपगोपीभिः समवेतो मुदान्वितः
उपगीयमानो ललितं गीतवाद्यविशारदैः ॥
198.m: Accompanied by the cowherds and gopīs, he drank with joy, / being sung to sweetly by those skilled in song and instrumental music.

198.s:
śramato 'tyantagharmāmbhaḥkaṇikāmauktikojjvalaḥ
āgaccha yamune snātum icchāmīty āha vihvalaḥ //
198.d:
श्रमतो ऽत्यन्तघर्माम्भःकणिकामौक्तिकोज्ज्वलः
आगच्छ यमुने स्नातुम् इच्छामीत्य् आह विह्वलः ॥
198.m: Brilliant with pearl-like droplets of heavy sweat from exhaustion, / agitated, [Balarāma] said: 'Come, Yamunā, I wish to bathe!'

198.s:
tasya vācaṃ nadī sā tu mattoktām avamanya vai
nājagāma tataḥ kruddho halaṃ jagrāha lāṅgalī //
198.d:
तस्य वाचं नदी सा तु मत्तोक्ताम् अवमन्य वै
नाजगाम ततः क्रुद्धो हलं जग्राह लाङ्गली ॥
198.m: Disregarding his word as the speech of a drunkard, the river / did not come; then, enraged, the plow-bearer seized his plow.

198.s:
gṛhītvā tāṃ taṭenaiva cakarṣa madavihvalaḥ
pāpe nāyāsi nāyāsi gamyatām icchayānyataḥ //
198.d:
गृहीत्वा तां तटेनैव चकर्ष मदविह्वलः
पापे नायासि नायासि गम्यताम् इच्छयान्यतः ॥
198.m: Catching her by her bank, overcome by intoxication, he dragged her: / 'Wicked one, you do not come, you do not come! Go elsewhere at your pleasure!'

198.s:
sā kṛṣṭā tena sahasā mārgaṃ saṃtyajya nimnagā
yatrāste baladevo 'sau plāvayām āsa tad vanam //
198.d:
सा कृष्टा तेन सहसा मार्गं संत्यज्य निम्नगा
यत्रास्ते बलदेवो ऽसौ प्लावयाम् आस तद् वनम् ॥
198.m: Dragged violently by him, the river abandoned her course / and flooded the forest where Baladeva was staying.

198.s:
śarīriṇī tathopetya trāsavihvalalocanā
prasīdety abravīd rāmaṃ muñca māṃ muśalāyudha //
198.d:
शरीरिणी तथोपेत्य त्रासविह्वललोचना
प्रसीदेत्य् अब्रवीद् रामं मुञ्च मां मुशलायुध ॥
198.m: Assuming a bodily form and approaching with eyes bewildered by fear, / she said to Rāma: 'Be gracious! Release me, O weapon-bearing pestle-wielder!'

198.s:
so 'bravīd avajānāsi mama śauryabalaṃ yadi
so 'haṃ tvāṃ halapātena nayiṣyāmi sahasradhā //
198.d:
सो ऽब्रवीद् अवजानासि मम शौर्यबलं यदि
सो ऽहं त्वां हलपातेन नयिष्यामि सहस्रधा ॥
198.m: He said: 'If you disrespect my valor and strength, / then I, with a strike of my plow, will divide you into a thousand parts!'

198.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktayātisaṃtrastas tayā nadyā prasāditaḥ
bhūbhāge plāvite tatra mumoca yamunāṃ balaḥ //
198.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्तयातिसंत्रस्तस् तया नद्या प्रसादितः
भूभागे प्लाविते तत्र मुमोच यमुनां बलः ॥
198.m: Vyāsa said: / Having been thus addressed, Bala, very terrified and propitiated by that river, / released the Yamunā once the region of land had been flooded there.

198.s:
tataḥ snātasya vai kāntir ājagāma mahāvane
avataṃsotpalaṃ cāru gṛhītvaikaṃ ca kuṇḍalam //
198.d:
ततः स्नातस्य वै कान्तिर् आजगाम महावने
अवतंसोत्पलं चारु गृहीत्वैकं च कुण्डलम् ॥
198.m: Then, after he had bathed in the great forest, Kānti indeed arrived, / taking a charming blue lotus for an ear-ornament and a single earring.

198.s:
varuṇaprahitāṃ cāsmai mālām amlānapaṅkajām
samudrārhe tathā vastre nīle lakṣmīr ayacchata //
198.d:
वरुणप्रहितां चास्मै मालाम् अम्लानपङ्कजाम्
समुद्रार्हे तथा वस्त्रे नीले लक्ष्मीर् अयच्छत ॥
198.m: And Lakṣmī gave him a garland of unfading lotuses sent by Varuṇa, / as well as two blue garments fit for the ocean.

198.s:
kṛtāvataṃsaḥ sa tadā cārukuṇḍalabhūṣitaḥ
nīlāmbaradharaḥ sragvī śuśubhe kāntisaṃyutaḥ //
198.d:
कृतावतंसः स तदा चारुकुण्डलभूषितः
नीलाम्बरधरः स्रग्वी शुशुभे कान्तिसंयुतः ॥
198.m: Adorned with the ear-ornament, embellished with the charming earring, / wearing the blue garments, adorned with the garland, he shone endowed with beauty.

198.s:
itthaṃ vibhūṣito reme tatra rāmas tadā vraje
māsadvayena yātaś ca punaḥ sa mathurāṃ purīm //
198.d:
इत्थं विभूषितो रेमे तत्र रामस् तदा व्रजे
मासद्वयेन यातश् च पुनः स मथुरां पुरीम् ॥
198.m: Thus adorned, Rāma then took delight there in Vraja; / and after two months he went back to the city of Mathurā.

198.s:
revatīṃ caiva tanayāṃ raivatasya mahīpateḥ
upayeme balas tasyāṃ jajñāte niśaṭholmukau //
198.d:
रेवतीं चैव तनयां रैवतस्य महीपतेः
उपयेमे बलस् तस्यां जज्ञाते निशठोल्मुकौ ॥
198.m: And Bala married Revatī, the daughter of King Raivata; / upon her Niśaṭha and Ulmuka were born.

199.s:
vyāsa uvāca
bhīṣmakaḥ kuṇḍine rājā vidarbhaviṣaye 'bhavat
rukmiṇī tasya duhitā rukmī caiva suto dvijāḥ //
199.d:
व्यास उवाच
भीष्मकः कुण्डिने राजा विदर्भविषये ऽभवत्
रुक्मिणी तस्य दुहिता रुक्मी चैव सुतो द्विजाः ॥
199.m: Vyāsa said: / Bhīṣmaka was king in Kuṇḍina in the country of Vidarbha; / his daughter was Rukmiṇī, and Rukmin was his son, O twice-born ones.

199.s:
rukmiṇīṃ cakame kṛṣṇaḥ sā ca taṃ cāruhāsinī
na dadau yācate caināṃ rukmī dveṣeṇa cakriṇe //
199.d:
रुक्मिणीं चकमे कृष्णः सा च तं चारुहासिनी
न ददौ याचते चैनां रुक्मी द्वेषेण चक्रिणे ॥
199.m: Kṛṣṇa desired Rukmiṇī, and she of charming smile desired him; / but when he asked for her, Rukmin did not give her to the wielder of the discus out of hatred.

199.s:
dadau sa śiśupālāya jarāsaṃdhapracoditaḥ
bhīṣmako rukmiṇā sārdhaṃ rukmiṇīm uruvikramaḥ //
199.d:
ददौ स शिशुपालाय जरासंधप्रचोदितः
भीष्मको रुक्मिणा सार्धं रुक्मिणीम् उरुविक्रमः ॥
199.m: Urged by Jarāsaṃdha, Bhīṣmaka of great prowess, / together with Rukmin, gave Rukmiṇī to Śiśupāla.

199.s:
vivāhārthaṃ tataḥ sarve jarāsaṃdhamukhā nṛpāḥ
bhīṣmakasya puraṃ jagmuḥ śiśupālaś ca kuṇḍinam //
199.d:
विवाहार्थं ततः सर्वे जरासंधमुखा नृपाः
भीष्मकस्य पुरं जग्मुः शिशुपालश् च कुण्डिनम् ॥
199.m: Then for the sake of the marriage, all the kings headed by Jarāsaṃdha / and Śiśupāla went to the city of Bhīṣmaka, to Kuṇḍina.

199.s:
kṛṣṇo 'pi balabhadrādyair yadubhiḥ parivāritaḥ
prayayau kuṇḍinaṃ draṣṭuṃ vivāhaṃ caidyabhūpateḥ //
199.d:
कृष्णो ऽपि बलभद्राद्यैर् यदुभिः परिवारितः
प्रययौ कुण्डिनं द्रष्टुं विवाहं चैद्यभूपतेः ॥
199.m: Kṛṣṇa too, surrounded by Balabhadra and the other Yadus, / set out for Kuṇḍina to see the marriage of the king of the Cedis.

199.s:
śvobhāvini vivāhe tu tāṃ kanyāṃ hṛtavān hariḥ
vipakṣabhāvam āsādya rāmādyeṣv eva bandhuṣu //
199.d:
श्वोभाविनि विवाहे तु तां कन्यां हृतवान् हरिः
विपक्षभावम् आसाद्य रामाद्येष्व् एव बन्धुषु ॥
199.m: When the wedding was to take place on the next day, Hari carried off that maiden, / while relatives like Rāma and others assumed the role of an opposing force.

199.s:
tataś ca pauṇḍrakaḥ śrīmān dantavaktro vidūrathaḥ
śiśupālo jarāsaṃdhaḥ śālvādyāś ca mahībhṛtaḥ //
199.d:
ततश् च पौण्ड्रकः श्रीमान् दन्तवक्त्रो विदूरथः
शिशुपालो जरासंधः शाल्वाद्याश् च महीभृतः ॥
199.m: And then the glorious Pauṇḍraka, Dantavaktra, Vidūratha, / Śiśupāla, Jarāsaṃdha, and kings such as Śālva,

199.s:
kupitās te hariṃ hantuṃ cakrur udyogam uttamam
nirjitāś ca samāgamya rāmādyair yadupuṃgavaiḥ //
199.d:
कुपितास् ते हरिं हन्तुं चक्रुर् उद्योगम् उत्तमम्
निर्जिताश् च समागम्य रामाद्यैर् यदुपुंगवैः ॥
199.m: enraged, made a supreme effort to kill Hari; / and coming together, they were completely defeated by the preeminent Yadus headed by Rāma.

199.s:
kuṇḍinaṃ na pravekṣyāmi ahatvā yudhi keśavam
kṛtvā pratijñāṃ rukmī ca hantuṃ kṛṣṇam abhidrutaḥ //
199.d:
कुण्डिनं न प्रवेक्ष्यामि अहत्वा युधि केशवम्
कृत्वा प्रतिज्ञां रुक्मी च हन्तुं कृष्णम् अभिद्रुतः ॥
199.m: "I will not enter Kuṇḍina without slaying Keśava in battle"— / having made this vow, Rukmin rushed forward to kill Kṛṣṇa.

199.s:
hatvā balaṃ sa nāgāśvapattisyandanasaṃkulam
nirjitaḥ pātitaś corvyāṃ līlayaiva sa cakriṇā //
199.d:
हत्वा बलं स नागाश्वपत्तिस्यन्दनसंकुलम्
निर्जितः पातितश् चोर्व्यां लीलयैव स चक्रिणा ॥
199.m: After destroying his army crowded with elephants, horses, foot-soldiers, and chariots, / he was effortlessly vanquished and thrown down to the earth by the wielder of the discus.

199.s:
nirjitya rukmiṇaṃ samyag upayeme sa rukmiṇīm
rākṣasena vidhānena saṃprāpto madhusūdanaḥ //
199.d:
निर्जित्य रुक्मिणं सम्यग् उपयेमे स रुक्मिणीम्
राक्षसेन विधानेन संप्राप्तो मधुसूदनः ॥
199.m: Having utterly defeated Rukmin, Madhusūdana, who had arrived, / married Rukmiṇī according to the rākṣasa rite.

199.s:
tasyāṃ jajñe ca pradyumno madanāṃśaḥ sa vīryavān
jahāra śambaro yaṃ vai yo jaghāna ca śambaram //
199.d:
तस्यां जज्ञे च प्रद्युम्नो मदनांशः स वीर्यवान्
जहार शम्बरो यं वै यो जघान च शम्बरम् ॥
199.m: And upon her was born Pradyumna of great valor, a portion of Madana, / whom Śambara indeed abducted and who slew Śambara.

200.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
śambareṇa hṛto vīraḥ pradyumnaḥ sa kathaṃ punaḥ
śambaraś ca mahāvīryaḥ pradyumnena kathaṃ hataḥ //
200.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
शम्बरेण हृतो वीरः प्रद्युम्नः स कथं पुनः
शम्बरश् च महावीर्यः प्रद्युम्नेन कथं हतः ॥
200.m: The sages said: / How was that hero Pradyumna abducted by Śambara, / and how was Śambara of great valor slain by Pradyumna?

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ṣaṣṭhe 'hni jātamātre tu pradyumnaṃ sūtikāgṛhāt
mamaiṣa hanteti dvijā hṛtavān kālaśambaraḥ //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
षष्ठे ऽह्नि जातमात्रे तु प्रद्युम्नं सूतिकागृहात्
ममैष हन्तेति द्विजा हृतवान् कालशम्बरः ॥
200.m: Vyāsa said: / On the sixth day, just after he was born, Kālaśambara abducted Pradyumna / from the lying-in chamber, O twice-born ones, thinking, "This is my slayer!"

200.s:
nītvā cikṣepa caivainaṃ grāho 'gre lavaṇārṇave
kallolajanitāvarte sughore makarālaye //
200.d:
नीत्वा चिक्षेप चैवैनं ग्राहो ऽग्रे लवणार्णवे
कल्लोलजनितावर्ते सुघोरे मकरालये ॥
200.m: And carrying him off, the monster cast him forward into the salt ocean, / into that terrible abode of sea-monsters with whirlpools produced by billowing waves.

200.s:
patitaṃ caiva tatraiko matsyo jagrāha bālakam
na mamāra ca tasyāpi jaṭharānaladīpitaḥ //
200.d:
पतितं चैव तत्रैको मत्स्यो जग्राह बालकम्
न ममार च तस्यापि जठरानलदीपितः ॥
200.m: And a fish seized the boy who had fallen there; / yet, blazing with the fire of the boy's belly, it did not die.

200.s:
matsyabandhaiś ca matsyo 'sau matsyair anyaiḥ saha dvijāḥ
ghātito 'suravaryāya śambarāya niveditaḥ //
200.d:
मत्स्यबन्धैश् च मत्स्यो ऽसौ मत्स्यैर् अन्यैः सह द्विजाः
घातितो ऽसुरवर्याय शम्बराय निवेदितः ॥
200.m: And that fish, along with other fish, O twice-born ones, / was killed by fishermen and presented to the foremost Asura, Śambara.

200.s:
tasya māyāvatī nāma patnī sarvagṛheśvarī
kārayām āsa sūdānām ādhipatyam aninditā //
200.d:
तस्य मायावती नाम पत्नी सर्वगृहेश्वरी
कारयाम् आस सूदानाम् आधिपत्यम् अनिन्दिता ॥
200.m: His wife named Māyāvatī, the mistress of the entire household, / blameless, exercised sovereignty over the cooks.

200.s:
dārite matsyajaṭhare dadṛśe sātiśobhanam
kumāraṃ manmathataror dagdhasya prathamāṅkuram //
200.d:
दारिते मत्स्यजठरे ददृशे सातिशोभनम्
कुमारं मन्मथतरोर् दग्धस्य प्रथमाङ्कुरम् ॥
200.m: When the belly of the fish was torn open, she saw an exceedingly handsome / boy, the first sprout of the burned tree of Manmatha.

200.s:
ko 'yaṃ katham ayaṃ matsyajaṭhare samupāgataḥ
ity evaṃ kautukāviṣṭāṃ tāṃ tanvīṃ prāha nāradaḥ //
200.d:
को ऽयं कथम् अयं मत्स्यजठरे समुपागतः
इत्य् एवं कौतुकाविष्टां तां तन्वीं प्राह नारदः ॥
200.m: "Who is this? How has he come into the belly of a fish?" / To that slender lady who was thus filled with wonder, Nārada spoke:

200.s:
nārada uvāca
ayaṃ samastajagatāṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakāriṇā
śambareṇa hṛtaḥ kṛṣṇatanayaḥ sūtikāgṛhāt //
200.d:
नारद उवाच
अयं समस्तजगतां सृष्टिसंहारकारिणा
शम्बरेण हृतः कृष्णतनयः सूतिकागृहात् ॥
200.m: Nārada said: / "This son of Kṛṣṇa has been abducted from the lying-in chamber / by Śambara, who brings about the creation and destruction of all the worlds.

200.s:
kṣiptaḥ samudre matsyena nigīrṇas te vaśaṃ gataḥ
nararatnam idaṃ subhru viśrabdhā paripālaya //
200.d:
क्षिप्तः समुद्रे मत्स्येन निगीर्णस् ते वशं गतः
नररत्नम् इदं सुभ्रु विश्रब्धा परिपालय ॥
200.m: Cast into the sea and swallowed by a fish, he has come under your power. / Protect this jewel among men with confidence, O fair-browed lady!"

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
nāradenaivam uktā sā pālayām āsa taṃ śiśum
bālyād evātirāgeṇa rūpātiśayamohitā //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
नारदेनैवम् उक्ता सा पालयाम् आस तं शिशुम्
बाल्याद् एवातिरागेण रूपातिशयमोहिता ॥
200.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus addressed by Nārada, she reared that child / from his childhood with intense affection, infatuated by the perfection of his beauty.

200.s:
sa yadā yauvanābhogabhūṣito 'bhūd dvijottamāḥ
sābhilāṣā tadā sā tu babhūva gajagāminī //
200.d:
स यदा यौवनाभोगभूषितो ऽभूद् द्विजोत्तमाः
साभिलाषा तदा सा तु बभूव गजगामिनी ॥
200.m: When he was adorned with the fullness of youth, O best of the twice-born, / then she, who walked like an elephant, was filled with desire.

200.s:
māyāvatī dadau cāsmai māyā sarvā mahātmane
pradyumnāyātmabhūtāya tannyastahṛdayekṣaṇā
prasajjantīṃ tu tām āha sa kārṣṇiḥ kamalalocanaḥ //
200.d:
मायावती ददौ चास्मै माया सर्वा महात्मने
प्रद्युम्नायात्मभूताय तन्न्यस्तहृदयेक्षणा
प्रसज्जन्तीं तु ताम् आह स कार्ष्णिः कमललोचनः ॥
200.m: And Māyāvatī imparted all illusory powers to the high-souled / Pradyumna, who had become her very self, her heart and eyes fixed upon him; / but to her who was clinging to him, the son of Kṛṣṇa, lotus-eyed, said:

200.s:
pradyumna uvāca
mātṛbhāvaṃ vihāyaiva kimarthaṃ vartase 'nyathā //
200.d:
प्रद्युम्न उवाच
मातृभावं विहायैव किमर्थं वर्तसे ऽन्यथा ॥
200.m: Pradyumna said: / "Why do you abandon maternal feelings and behave otherwise?"

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
sā cāsmai kathayām āsa na putras tvaṃ mameti vai
tanayaṃ tvām ayaṃ viṣṇor hṛtavān kālaśambaraḥ //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
सा चास्मै कथयाम् आस न पुत्रस् त्वं ममेति वै
तनयं त्वाम् अयं विष्णोर् हृतवान् कालशम्बरः ॥
200.m: Vyāsa said: / And she told him: "You are indeed not my son; / Kālaśambara carried you off, the son of Viṣṇu.

200.s:
kṣiptaḥ samudre matsyasya saṃprāpto jaṭharān mayā
sā tu roditi te mātā kāntādyāpy ativatsalā //
200.d:
क्षिप्तः समुद्रे मत्स्यस्य संप्राप्तो जठरान् मया
सा तु रोदिति ते माता कान्ताद्याप्य् अतिवत्सला ॥
200.m: You were thrown into the ocean and obtained by me from the belly of a fish; / but that mother of yours, deeply affectionate, still weeps for her beloved."

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktaḥ śambaraṃ yuddhe pradyumnaḥ sa samāhvayat
krodhākulīkṛtamanā yuyudhe ca mahābalaḥ //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्तः शम्बरं युद्धे प्रद्युम्नः स समाह्वयत्
क्रोधाकुलीकृतमना युयुधे च महाबलः ॥
200.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus spoken to, Pradyumna challenged Śambara in battle; / with his mind agitated by anger, that one of great strength fought.

200.s:
hatvā sainyam aśeṣaṃ tu tasya daityasya mādhaviḥ
sapta māyā vyatikramya māyāṃ saṃyuyuje 'ṣṭamīm //
200.d:
हत्वा सैन्यम् अशेषं तु तस्य दैत्यस्य माधविः
सप्त माया व्यतिक्रम्य मायां संयुयुजे ऽष्टमीम् ॥
200.m: Having slain the entire army of that Daitya, the descendant of Madhu, / having overcome seven illusory arts, employed the eighth illusory art.

200.s:
tayā jaghāna taṃ daityaṃ māyayā kālaśambaram
utpatya ca tayā sārdham ājagāma pituḥ puram //
200.d:
तया जघान तं दैत्यं मायया कालशम्बरम्
उत्पत्य च तया सार्धम् आजगाम पितुः पुरम् ॥
200.m: With that illusory power he slew that Daitya Kālaśambara; / and flying up with her, he went to his father's city.

200.s:
antaḥpure ca patitaṃ māyāvatyā samanvitam
taṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭasaṃkalpā babhūvuḥ kṛṣṇayoṣitaḥ
rukmiṇī cābravīt premṇā āsaktadṛṣṭir aninditā //
200.d:
अन्तःपुरे च पतितं मायावत्या समन्वितम्
तं दृष्ट्वा हृष्टसंकल्पा बभूवुः कृष्णयोषितः
रुक्मिणी चाब्रवीत् प्रेम्णा आसक्तदृष्टिर् अनिन्दिता ॥
200.m: Seeing him who had descended into the inner chambers together with Māyāvatī, / the wives of Kṛṣṇa became joyful in mind; / and Rukmiṇī, blameless, said with love, her gaze fixed upon him:

200.s:
rukmiṇy uvāca
dhanyāyāḥ khalv ayaṃ putro vartate navayauvane
asmin vayasi putro me pradyumno yadi jīvati //
200.d:
रुक्मिण्य् उवाच
धन्यायाः खल्व् अयं पुत्रो वर्तते नवयौवने
अस्मिन् वयसि पुत्रो मे प्रद्युम्नो यदि जीवति ॥
200.m: Rukmiṇī said: / "Fortunate indeed is the woman whose son this is, now in the prime of fresh youth; / my son Pradyumna would be at this age, if he is alive.

200.s:
sabhāgyā jananī vatsa tvayā kāpi vibhūṣitā
athavā yādṛśaḥ sneho mama yādṛg vapuś ca te
harer apatyaṃ suvyaktaṃ bhavān vatsa bhaviṣyati //
200.d:
सभाग्या जननी वत्स त्वया कापि विभूषिता
अथवा यादृशः स्नेहो मम यादृग् वपुश् च ते
हरेर् अपत्यं सुव्यक्तं भवान् वत्स भविष्यति ॥
200.m: Some mother, O dear child, has been made fortunate, adorned by you! / Or, judging by the love that is mine and by your form, / you are very clearly Hari's offspring, my dear child!"

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
etasminn antare prāptaḥ saha kṛṣṇena nāradaḥ
antaḥpuravarāṃ devīṃ rukmiṇīṃ prāha harṣitaḥ //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे प्राप्तः सह कृष्णेन नारदः
अन्तःपुरवरां देवीं रुक्मिणीं प्राह हर्षितः ॥
200.m: Vyāsa said: / In the meantime Nārada arrived together with Kṛṣṇa; / delighted, he spoke to Queen Rukmiṇī, the best of the inner chamber:

200.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
eṣa te tanayaḥ subhru hatvā śambaram āgataḥ
hṛto yenābhavat pūrvaṃ putras te sūtikāgṛhāt //
200.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
एष ते तनयः सुभ्रु हत्वा शम्बरम् आगतः
हृतो येनाभवत् पूर्वं पुत्रस् ते सूतिकागृहात् ॥
200.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / "O fair-browed lady, this is your son who has returned after slaying Śambara, / by whom your son was previously abducted from the lying-in chamber.

200.s:
iyaṃ māyāvatī bhāryā tanayasyāsya te satī
śambarasya na bhāryeyaṃ śrūyatām atra kāraṇam //
200.d:
इयं मायावती भार्या तनयस्यास्य ते सती
शम्बरस्य न भार्येयं श्रूयताम् अत्र कारणम् ॥
200.m: This virtuous Māyāvatī is the wife of this son of yours; / she is not Śambara's wife. Hear the reason for this:

200.s:
manmathe tu gate nāśaṃ tadudbhavaparāyaṇā
śambaraṃ mohayām āsa māyārūpeṇa rukmiṇi //
200.d:
मन्मथे तु गते नाशं तदुद्भवपरायणा
शम्बरं मोहयाम् आस मायारूपेण रुक्मिणि ॥
200.m: When Manmatha met his destruction, she, intent on his rebirth, / deluded Śambara with an illusory form, O Rukmiṇī.

200.s:
vivāhādyupabhogeṣu rūpaṃ māyāmayaṃ śubham
darśayām āsa daityasya tasyeyaṃ madirekṣaṇā //
200.d:
विवाहाद्युपभोगेषु रूपं मायामयं शुभम्
दर्शयाम् आस दैत्यस्य तस्येयं मदिरेक्षणा ॥
200.m: In marriage and other pleasures, she of intoxicating eyes / displayed to that Daitya an illusory, auspicious form.

200.s:
kāmo 'vatīrṇaḥ putras te tasyeyaṃ dayitā ratiḥ
viśaṅkā nātra kartavyā snuṣeyaṃ tava śobhanā //
200.d:
कामो ऽवतीर्णः पुत्रस् ते तस्येयं दयिता रतिः
विशङ्का नात्र कर्तव्या स्नुषेयं तव शोभना ॥
200.m: Your son is Kāma descended, and this is his beloved Rati; / no doubt should be entertained here. She is your fair daughter-in-law."

200.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tato harṣasamāviṣṭau rukmiṇīkeśavau tadā
nagarī ca samastā sā sādhu sādhv ity abhāṣata //
200.d:
व्यास उवाच
ततो हर्षसमाविष्टौ रुक्मिणीकेशवौ तदा
नगरी च समस्ता सा साधु साध्व् इत्य् अभाषत ॥
200.m:
Vyāsa said:
Then Rukmiṇī and Keśava were filled with joy, / and the whole city cried out, “Well done! Well done!”

200.s:
ciraṃ naṣṭena putreṇa saṃgatāṃ prekṣya rukmiṇīm
avāpa vismayaṃ sarvo dvāravatyāṃ janas tadā //
200.d:
चिरं नष्टेन पुत्रेण संगतां प्रेक्ष्य रुक्मिणीम्
अवाप विस्मयं सर्वो द्वारवत्यां जनस् तदा ॥
200.m: Seeing Rukmiṇī reunited with her long-lost son, / all the people in Dvāravatī were filled with wonder.

201.s:
vyāsa uvāca
cārudeṣṇaṃ sudeṣṇaṃ ca cārudehaṃ ca śobhanam
suṣeṇaṃ cāruguptaṃ ca bhadracāruṃ tathāparam //
201.d:
व्यास उवाच
चारुदेष्णं सुदेष्णं च चारुदेहं च शोभनम्
सुषेणं चारुगुप्तं च भद्रचारुं तथापरम् ॥
201.m:
Vyāsa said:
Cārudeṣṇa, Sudeṣṇa, the handsome Cārudeha, / Suṣeṇa, Cārugupta, and another, Bhadracāru,

201.s:
cāruvindaṃ sucāruṃ ca cāruṃ ca balināṃ varam
rukmiṇy ajanayat putrān kanyāṃ cārumatīṃ tathā //
201.d:
चारुविन्दं सुचारुं च चारुं च बलिनां वरम्
रुक्मिण्य् अजनयत् पुत्रान् कन्यां चारुमतीं तथा ॥
201.m: Cāruvinda, Sucāru, and Cāru, best of the strong— / Rukmiṇī bore these sons, and also a daughter, Cārumatī.

201.s:
anyāś ca bhāryāḥ kṛṣṇasya babhūvuḥ sapta śobhanāḥ
kālindī mitravindā ca satyā nāgnajitī tathā //
201.d:
अन्याश् च भार्याः कृष्णस्य बभूवुः सप्त शोभनाः
कालिन्दी मित्रविन्दा च सत्या नाग्नजिती तथा ॥
201.m: And Kṛṣṇa had seven other beautiful wives: / Kālindī, Mitravindā, and Satyā, the daughter of Nagnajit,

201.s:
devī jāmbavatī cāpi sadā tuṣṭā tu rohiṇī
madrarājasutā cānyā suśīlā śīlamaṇḍalā //
201.d:
देवी जाम्बवती चापि सदा तुष्टा तु रोहिणी
मद्रराजसुता चान्या सुशीला शीलमण्डला ॥
201.m: and the divine Jāmbavatī, and Rohiṇī, who was ever cheerful, / and another, the princess of Madra, virtuous and endowed with all good conduct,

201.s:
sātrājitī satyabhāmā lakṣmaṇā cāruhāsinī
ṣoḍaśātra sahasrāṇi strīṇām anyāni cakriṇaḥ //
201.d:
सात्राजिती सत्यभामा लक्ष्मणा चारुहासिनी
षोडशात्र सहस्राणि स्त्रीणाम् अन्यानि चक्रिणः ॥
201.m: Satyabhāmā, the daughter of Satrājit, and the sweet-smiling Lakṣmaṇā. / In addition to these, the wielder of the discus had sixteen thousand women.

201.s:
pradyumno 'pi mahāvīryo rukmiṇas tanayāṃ śubhām
svayaṃvarasthāṃ jagrāha sāpi taṃ tanayaṃ hareḥ //
201.d:
प्रद्युम्नो ऽपि महावीर्यो रुक्मिणस् तनयां शुभाम्
स्वयंवरस्थां जग्राह सापि तं तनयं हरेः ॥
201.m: The mighty Pradyumna too took the fair daughter of Rukmin / at her svayaṃvara, and she chose that son of Hari.

201.s:
tasyām asyābhavat putro mahābalaparākramaḥ
aniruddho raṇe ruddho vīryodadhir ariṃdamaḥ //
201.d:
तस्याम् अस्याभवत् पुत्रो महाबलपराक्रमः
अनिरुद्धो रणे रुद्धो वीर्योदधिर् अरिंदमः ॥
201.m: Upon her he fathered a son of great strength and valor, / Aniruddha, unobstructed in battle, an ocean of prowess, a tamer of foes.

201.s:
tasyāpi rukmiṇaḥ pautrīṃ varayām āsa keśavaḥ
dauhitrāya dadau rukmī spardhayann api śauriṇā //
201.d:
तस्यापि रुक्मिणः पौत्रीं वरयाम् आस केशवः
दौहित्राय ददौ रुक्मी स्पर्धयन्न् अपि शौरिणा ॥
201.m: For him Keśava chose the granddaughter of Rukmin; / Rukmin gave her to his daughter’s son, even while rivaling Śauri.

201.s:
tasyā vivāhe rāmādyā yādavā hariṇā saha
rukmiṇo nagaraṃ jagmur nāmnā bhojakaṭaṃ dvijāḥ //
201.d:
तस्या विवाहे रामाद्या यादवा हरिणा सह
रुक्मिणो नगरं जग्मुर् नाम्ना भोजकटं द्विजाः ॥
201.m: For his wedding, O twice-born ones, the Yādavas headed by Rāma, together with Hari, / went to Rukmin’s city, named Bhojakaṭa.

201.s:
vivāhe tatra nirvṛtte prādyumneḥ sumahātmanaḥ
kaliṅgarājapramukhā rukmiṇaṃ vākyam abruvan //
201.d:
विवाहे तत्र निर्वृत्ते प्राद्युम्नेः सुमहात्मनः
कलिङ्गराजप्रमुखा रुक्मिणं वाक्यम् अब्रुवन् ॥
201.m: When the marriage of Pradyumna’s high-souled son was concluded there, / [the kings] headed by the king of Kaliṅga addressed words to Rukmin:

201.s:
kaliṅgādaya ūcuḥ
anakṣajño halī dyūte tathāsya vyasanaṃ mahat
tan nayāmo balaṃ tasmād dyūtenaiva mahādyute //
201.d:
कलिङ्गादय ऊचुः
अनक्षज्ञो हली द्यूते तथास्य व्यसनं महत्
तन् नयामो बलं तस्माद् द्यूतेनैव महाद्युते ॥
201.m:
The Kaliṅga king and others said:
“The plow-wielder does not know dice, yet he has a great passion for gambling; / therefore, O greatly radiant one, let us defeat Bala by dice alone!”

201.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tatheti tān āha nṛpān rukmī balasamanvitaḥ
sabhāyāṃ saha rāmeṇa cakre dyūtaṃ ca vai tadā //
201.d:
व्यास उवाच
तथेति तान् आह नृपान् रुक्मी बलसमन्वितः
सभायां सह रामेण चक्रे द्यूतं च वै तदा ॥
201.m:
Vyāsa said:
“So be it,” Rukmin, endowed with might, said to those kings, / and then engaged in a game of dice with Rāma in the assembly hall.

201.s:
sahasram ekaṃ niṣkāṇāṃ rukmiṇā vijito balaḥ
dvitīye divase cānyat sahasraṃ rukmiṇā jitaḥ //
201.d:
सहस्रम् एकं निष्काणां रुक्मिणा विजितो बलः
द्वितीये दिवसे चान्यत् सहस्रं रुक्मिणा जितः ॥
201.m: A thousand niṣkas were won from Bala by Rukmin; / on the second day, another thousand was won by Rukmin.

201.s:
tato daśa sahasrāṇi niṣkāṇāṃ paṇam ādade
balabhadraprapannāni rukmī dyūtavidāṃ varaḥ //
201.d:
ततो दश सहस्राणि निष्काणां पणम् आददे
बलभद्रप्रपन्नानि रुक्मी द्यूतविदां वरः ॥
201.m: Then Rukmin, best among those skilled in dice, / accepted a wager of ten thousand niṣkas offered by Balabhadra.

201.s:
tato jahāsātha balaṃ kaliṅgādhipatir dvijāḥ
dantān vidarśayan mūḍho rukmī cāha madoddhataḥ //
201.d:
ततो जहासाथ बलं कलिङ्गाधिपतिर् द्विजाः
दन्तान् विदर्शयन् मूढो रुक्मी चाह मदोद्धतः ॥
201.m: Then, O twice-born ones, the foolish king of Kaliṅga laughed at Bala, / showing his teeth, and Rukmin, haughty with pride, said:

201.s:
rukmy uvāca
avidyo 'yaṃ mahādyūte balabhadraḥ parājitaḥ
mṛṣaivākṣāvalepatvād yo 'yaṃ mene 'kṣakovidam //
201.d:
रुक्म्य् उवाच
अविद्यो ऽयं महाद्यूते बलभद्रः पराजितः
मृषैवाक्षावलेपत्वाद् यो ऽयं मेने ऽक्षकोविदम् ॥
201.m:
Rukmin said:
“This Balabhadra, who is unskilled in the great game of dice, has been defeated! / In vain, out of vanity regarding the dice, did he deem himself skilled in dice!”

201.s:
dṛṣṭvā kaliṅgarājaṃ tu prakāśadaśanānanam
rukmiṇaṃ cāpi durvākyaṃ kopaṃ cakre halāyudhaḥ //
201.d:
दृष्ट्वा कलिङ्गराजं तु प्रकाशदशनाननम्
रुक्मिणं चापि दुर्वाक्यं कोपं चक्रे हलायुधः ॥
201.m: Seeing the king of Kaliṅga with his teeth bared in a grin, / and hearing Rukmin’s abusive words, the plow-armed one grew enraged.

201.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tataḥ kopaparītātmā niṣkakoṭiṃ halāyudhaḥ
glahaṃ jagrāha rukmī ca tatas tv akṣān apātayat //
201.d:
व्यास उवाच
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा निष्ककोटिं हलायुधः
ग्लहं जग्राह रुक्मी च ततस् त्व् अक्षान् अपातयत् ॥
201.m:
Vyāsa said:
Then, his mind seized by rage, the plow-armed one staked / a crore of niṣkas, and Rukmin cast the dice.

201.s:
ajayad baladevo 'tha prāhoccais taṃ jitaṃ mayā
mameti rukmī prāhoccair alīkoktair alaṃ balam //
201.d:
अजयद् बलदेवो ऽथ प्राहोच्चैस् तं जितं मया
ममेति रुक्मी प्राहोच्चैर् अलीकोक्तैर् अलं बलम् ॥
201.m: Baladeva won, and said aloud: “I have won!” / “It is mine!” Rukmin said loudly, “enough of your false claims, Bala!”

201.s:
tvayokto 'yaṃ glahaḥ satyaṃ na mamaiṣo 'numoditaḥ
evaṃ tvayā ced vijitaṃ na mayā vijitaṃ katham //
201.d:
त्वयोक्तो ऽयं ग्लहः सत्यं न ममैषो ऽनुमोदितः
एवं त्वया चेद् विजितं न मया विजितं कथम् ॥
201.m: “This wager was declared by you, true, but it was not agreed to by me. / If you have won in this manner, why have I not won?”

201.s:
tato 'ntarikṣe vāg uccaiḥ prāha gambhīranādinī
baladevasya taṃ kopaṃ vardhayantī mahātmanaḥ //
201.d:
ततो ऽन्तरिक्षे वाग् उच्चैः प्राह गम्भीरनादिनी
बलदेवस्य तं कोपं वर्धयन्ती महात्मनः ॥
201.m: Then a voice in the sky spoke aloud in a deep roar, / increasing the wrath of the high-souled Baladeva:

201.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
jitaṃ tu baladevena rukmiṇā bhāṣitaṃ mṛṣā
anuktvā vacanaṃ kiṃcit kṛtaṃ bhavati karmaṇā //
201.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
जितं तु बलदेवेन रुक्मिणा भाषितं मृषा
अनुक्त्वा वचनं किंचित् कृतं भवति कर्मणा ॥
201.m:
The voice in the sky said:
“It was indeed won by Baladeva; Rukmin has spoken falsely. / Even without uttering a word, [consent] is established by action.”

201.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tato balaḥ samutthāya krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
jaghānāṣṭāpadenaiva rukmiṇaṃ sa mahābalaḥ //
201.d:
व्यास उवाच
ततो बलः समुत्थाय क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः
जघानाष्टापदेनैव रुक्मिणं स महाबलः ॥
201.m:
Vyāsa said:
Then Bala arose, his eyes bloodshot with rage, / and that mighty one struck Rukmin dead with the gaming board itself.

201.s:
kaliṅgarājaṃ cādāya visphurantaṃ balād balaḥ
babhañja dantān kupito yaiḥ prakāśaṃ jahāsa saḥ //
201.d:
कलिङ्गराजं चादाय विस्फुरन्तं बलाद् बलः
बभञ्ज दन्तान् कुपितो यैः प्रकाशं जहास सः ॥
201.m: And violently seizing the trembling king of Kaliṅga, / Bala, in his fury, smashed the teeth with which he had openly laughed.

201.s:
ākṛṣya ca mahāstambhaṃ jātarūpamayaṃ balaḥ
jaghāna ye tatpakṣās tān bhūbhṛtaḥ kupito balaḥ //
201.d:
आकृष्य च महास्तम्भं जातरूपमयं बलः
जघान ये तत्पक्षास् तान् भूभृतः कुपितो बलः ॥
201.m: Uprooting a massive pillar made of gold, / the enraged Bala struck down the kings who were on his side.

201.s:
tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ palāyanaparaṃ dvijāḥ
tad rājamaṇḍalaṃ sarvaṃ babhūva kupite bale //
201.d:
ततो हाहाकृतं सर्वं पलायनपरं द्विजाः
तद् राजमण्डलं सर्वं बभूव कुपिते बले ॥
201.m: Then a cry of woe arose, and all of them took to flight, O twice-born ones; / that entire circle of kings fled when Bala was enraged.

201.s:
balena nihataṃ śrutvā rukmiṇaṃ madhusūdanaḥ
novāca vacanaṃ kiṃcid rukmiṇībalayor bhayāt //
201.d:
बलेन निहतं श्रुत्वा रुक्मिणं मधुसूदनः
नोवाच वचनं किंचिद् रुक्मिणीबलयोर् भयात् ॥
201.m: Hearing that Rukmin had been slain by Bala, Madhusūdana / said not a word, out of fear for both Rukmiṇī and Bala.

201.s:
tato 'niruddham ādāya kṛtodvāhaṃ dvijottamāḥ
dvārakām ājagāmātha yaducakraṃ sakeśavam //
201.d:
ततो ऽनिरुद्धम् आदाय कृतोद्वाहं द्विजोत्तमाः
द्वारकाम् आजगामाथ यदुचक्रं सकेशवम् ॥
201.m: Then, taking Aniruddha, who had concluded his marriage, O best of the twice-born, / the host of the Yadus returned to Dvārakā along with Keśava.

202.s:
vyāsa uvāca
dvāravatyāṃ tataḥ śauriṃ śakras tribhuvaneśvaraḥ
ājagāmātha munayo mattairāvatapṛṣṭhagaḥ //
202.d:
व्यास उवाच
द्वारवत्यां ततः शौरिं शक्रस् त्रिभुवनेश्वरः
आजगामाथ मुनयो मत्तैरावतपृष्ठगः ॥
202.m:
Vyāsa said:
Then Śakra, the lord of the three worlds, mounted on the rutting Airāvata, / came to Śauri in Dvāravatī, O sages.

202.s:
praviśya dvārakāṃ so 'tha samīpe ca hares tadā
kathayām āsa daityasya narakasya viceṣṭitam //
202.d:
प्रविश्य द्वारकां सो ऽथ समीपे च हरेस् तदा
कथयाम् आस दैत्यस्य नरकस्य विचेष्टितम् ॥
202.m: Entering Dvārakā, he then approached Hari / and recounted the deeds of the Daitya Naraka:

202.s:
indra uvāca
tvayā nāthena devānāṃ manuṣyatve 'pi tiṣṭhatā
praśamaṃ sarvaduḥkhāni nītāni madhusūdana //
202.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
त्वया नाथेन देवानां मनुष्यत्वे ऽपि तिष्ठता
प्रशमं सर्वदुःखानि नीतानि मधुसूदन ॥
202.m:
Indra said:
“With you as protector of the gods, even while dwelling in human form, / all afflictions have been brought to an end, O Madhusūdana.

202.s:
tapasvijanarakṣāyai so 'riṣṭo dhenukas tathā
pralambādyās tathā keśī te sarve nihatās tvayā //
202.d:
तपस्विजनरक्षायै सो ऽरिष्टो धेनुकस् तथा
प्रलम्बाद्यास् तथा केशी ते सर्वे निहतास् त्वया ॥
202.m: For the protection of ascetics, Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, / Pralamba and the rest, and Keśin—all of them have been slain by you.

202.s:
kaṃsaḥ kuvalayāpīḍaḥ pūtanā bālaghātinī
nāśaṃ nītās tvayā sarve ye 'nye jagadupadravāḥ //
202.d:
कंसः कुवलयापीडः पूतना बालघातिनी
नाशं नीतास् त्वया सर्वे ये ऽन्ये जगदुपद्रवाः ॥
202.m: Kaṃsa, Kuvalayāpīḍa, and Pūtanā the slayer of children, / and all other afflictions of the world have been brought to destruction by you.

202.s:
yuṣmaddordaṇḍasaṃbuddhiparitrāte jagattraye
yajñe yajñahaviḥ prāśya tṛptiṃ yānti divaukasaḥ //
202.d:
युष्मद्दोर्दण्डसंबुद्धिपरित्राते जगत्त्रये
यज्ञे यज्ञहविः प्राश्य तृप्तिं यान्ति दिवौकसः ॥
202.m: When the three worlds are guarded by your formidable arms, / the dwellers of heaven attain satisfaction by consuming the sacrificial oblation at sacrifices.

202.s:
so 'haṃ sāṃpratam āyāto yannimittaṃ janārdana
tac chrutvā tatpratīkāraprayatnaṃ kartum arhasi //
202.d:
सो ऽहं सांप्रतम् आयातो यन्निमित्तं जनार्दन
तच् छ्रुत्वा तत्प्रतीकारप्रयत्नं कर्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
202.m: The cause for which I have now come, O Janārdana— / hear it, and deign to make an effort to remedy it.

202.s:
bhaumo 'yaṃ narako nāma prāgjyotiṣapureśvaraḥ
karoti sarvabhūtānām apaghātam ariṃdama //
202.d:
भौमो ऽयं नरको नाम प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरेश्वरः
करोति सर्वभूतानाम् अपघातम् अरिंदम ॥
202.m: This son of the Earth, named Naraka, ruler of the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, / brings destruction to all living beings, O tamer of foes.

202.s:
devasiddhasurādīnāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ ca janārdana
hatvā tu so 'suraḥ kanyā rurodha nijamandire //
202.d:
देवसिद्धसुरादीनां नृपाणां च जनार्दन
हत्वा तु सो ऽसुरः कन्या रुरोध निजमन्दिरे ॥
202.m: Having slain gods, siddhas, asuras, and kings, O Janārdana, / that asura has confined their maidens in his own palace.

202.s:
chattraṃ yat salilasrāvi taj jahāra pracetasaḥ
mandarasya tathā śṛṅgaṃ hṛtavān maṇiparvatam //
202.d:
छत्त्रं यत् सलिलस्रावि तज् जहार प्रचेतसः
मन्दरस्य तथा शृङ्गं हृतवान् मणिपर्वतम् ॥
202.m: He stole the umbrella of Pracetas which sheds water, / and he took the peak of Mandara, the jeweled mountain.

202.s:
amṛtasrāviṇī divye mātur me 'mṛtakuṇḍale
jahāra so 'suro 'dityā vāñchaty airāvataṃ dvipam //
202.d:
अमृतस्राविणी दिव्ये मातुर् मे ऽमृतकुण्डले
जहार सो ऽसुरो ऽदित्या वाञ्छत्य् ऐरावतं द्विपम् ॥
202.m: That asura stole the two divine earrings of my mother Aditi, dripping with nectar, / and he covets the elephant Airāvata.

202.s:
durnītam etad govinda mayā tasya tavoditam
yad atra pratikartavyaṃ tat svayaṃ parimṛśyatām //
202.d:
दुर्नीतम् एतद् गोविन्द मया तस्य तवोदितम्
यद् अत्र प्रतिकर्तव्यं तत् स्वयं परिमृश्यताम् ॥
202.m: This misconduct of his has been related to you by me, O Govinda; / consider yourself what should be done as a remedy in this matter.”

202.s:
vyāsa uvāca
iti śrutvā smitaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān devakīsutaḥ
gṛhītvā vāsavaṃ haste samuttasthau varāsanāt //
202.d:
व्यास उवाच
इति श्रुत्वा स्मितं कृत्वा भगवान् देवकीसुतः
गृहीत्वा वासवं हस्ते समुत्तस्थौ वरासनात् ॥
202.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having heard this and smiled, the blessed son of Devakī / took Vāsava by the hand and rose from his splendid seat.

202.s:
saṃcintitam upāruhya garuḍaṃ gaganecaram
satyabhāmāṃ samāropya yayau prāgjyotiṣaṃ puram //
202.d:
संचिन्तितम् उपारुह्य गरुडं गगनेचरम्
सत्यभामां समारोप्य ययौ प्राग्ज्योतिषं पुरम् ॥
202.m: Mounting the sky-wandering Garuḍa, summoned by thought, / and taking Satyabhāmā with him, he set out for the city of Prāgjyotiṣa.

202.s:
āruhyairāvataṃ nāgaṃ śakro 'pi tridaśālayam
tato jagāma sumanāḥ paśyatāṃ dvārakaukasām //
202.d:
आरुह्यैरावतं नागं शक्रो ऽपि त्रिदशालयम्
ततो जगाम सुमनाः पश्यतां द्वारकौकसाम् ॥
202.m: Śakra too, mounting the elephant Airāvata, / then went to the abode of the thirty gods with a joyful mind, as the residents of Dvārakā looked on.

202.s:
prāgjyotiṣapurasyāsya samantāc chatayojanam
ācitaṃ bhairavaiḥ pāśaiḥ parasainyanivāraṇe //
202.d:
प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरस्यास्य समन्ताच् छतयोजनम्
आचितं भैरवैः पाशैः परसैन्यनिवारणे ॥
202.m: For a hundred yojanas all around this city of Prāgjyotiṣa, / it was covered with terrible snares to ward off enemy armies.

202.s:
tāṃś ciccheda hariḥ pāśān kṣiptvā cakraṃ sudarśanam
tato muraḥ samuttasthau taṃ jaghāna ca keśavaḥ //
202.d:
तांश् चिच्छेद हरिः पाशान् क्षिप्त्वा चक्रं सुदर्शनम्
ततो मुरः समुत्तस्थौ तं जघान च केशवः ॥
202.m: Hari cut those snares, hurling the Sudarśana discus; / then Mura arose, and Keśava slew him.

202.s:
muros tu tanayān sapta sahasrās tāṃs tato hariḥ
cakradhārāgninirdagdhāṃś cakāra śalabhān iva //
202.d:
मुरोस् तु तनयान् सप्त सहस्रास् तांस् ततो हरिः
चक्रधाराग्निनिर्दग्धांश् चकार शलभान् इव ॥
202.m:
Then Hari burned Mura's seven thousand sons
with the fire of his discus's edge, like moths.

202.s:
hatvā muraṃ hayagrīvaṃ tathā pañcajanaṃ dvijāḥ
prāgjyotiṣapuraṃ dhīmāṃs tvarāvān samupādravat //
202.d:
हत्वा मुरं हयग्रीवं तथा पञ्चजनं द्विजाः
प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरं धीमांस् त्वरावान् समुपाद्रवत् ॥
202.m:
Having slain Mura, Hayagrīva, and likewise Pañcajana, O twice-born ones,
the wise and swift one rushed toward the city of Prāgjyotiṣa.

202.s:
narakenāsya tatrābhūn mahāsainyena saṃyugaḥ
kṛṣṇasya yatra govindo jaghne daityān sahasraśaḥ //
202.d:
नरकेनास्य तत्राभून् महासैन्येन संयुगः
कृष्णस्य यत्र गोविन्दो जघ्ने दैत्यान् सहस्रशः ॥
202.m:
There took place a battle with Naraka and his vast army,
in which Govinda, Kṛṣṇa, slew Daityas by the thousands.

202.s:
śastrāstravarṣaṃ muñcantaṃ sa bhaumaṃ narakaṃ balī
kṣiptvā cakraṃ dvidhā cakre cakrī daiteyacakrahā //
202.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रवर्षं मुञ्चन्तं स भौमं नरकं बली
क्षिप्त्वा चक्रं द्विधा चक्रे चक्री दैतेयचक्रहा ॥
202.m:
Hurling his discus at Naraka, son of the Earth, who was discharging a rain of weapons and missiles,
the mighty wielder of the discus, slayer of the host of Daityas, cleaved him in two.

202.s:
hate tu narake bhūmir gṛhītvāditikuṇḍale
upatasthe jagannāthaṃ vākyaṃ cedam athābravīt //
202.d:
हते तु नरके भूमिर् गृहीत्वादितिकुण्डले
उपतस्थे जगन्नाथं वाक्यं चेदम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
202.m:
When Naraka was slain, the Earth took Aditi's two earrings,
approached the Lord of the World, and spoke these words:

202.s:
dharaṇy uvāca
yadāham uddhṛtā nātha tvayā śūkaramūrtinā
tvatsaṃsparśabhavaḥ putras tadāyaṃ mayy ajāyata //
202.d:
धरण्य् उवाच
यदाहम् उद्धृता नाथ त्वया शूकरमूर्तिना
त्वत्संस्पर्शभवः पुत्रस् तदायं मय्य् अजायत ॥
202.m:
Dharaṇī said:
When I was lifted up by you in the form of a boar, O Lord,
then this son was born in me from contact with you.

202.s:
so 'yaṃ tvayaiva datto me tvayaiva vinipātitaḥ
gṛhāṇa kuṇḍale ceme pālayāsya ca saṃtatim //
202.d:
सो ऽयं त्वयैव दत्तो मे त्वयैव विनिपातितः
गृहाण कुण्डले चेमे पालयास्य च संततिम् ॥
202.m:
He was given to me by you alone, and by you alone he has been struck down.
Take these two earrings, and protect his progeny.

202.s:
bhārāvataraṇārthāya mamaiva bhagavān imam
aṃśena lokam āyātaḥ prasādasumukha prabho //
202.d:
भारावतरणार्थाय ममैव भगवान् इमम्
अंशेन लोकम् आयातः प्रसादसुमुख प्रभो ॥
202.m:
For the purpose of removing my burden, the Blessed One has come to this world
with a portion [of himself], O Lord gracious of countenance!

202.s:
tvaṃ kartā ca vikartā ca saṃhartā prabhavo 'vyayaḥ
jagatsvarūpo yaś ca tvaṃ stūyase 'cyuta kiṃ mayā //
202.d:
त्वं कर्ता च विकर्ता च संहर्ता प्रभवो ऽव्ययः
जगत्स्वरूपो यश् च त्वं स्तूयसे ऽच्युत किं मया ॥
202.m:
You are the creator, the transformer, the destroyer, the origin, imperishable;
you whose form is the world, how can you be praised by me, O Acyuta?

202.s:
vyāpī vyāpyaḥ kriyā kartā kāryaṃ ca bhagavān sadā
sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā stūyase 'cyuta kiṃ mayā //
202.d:
व्यापी व्याप्यः क्रिया कर्ता कार्यं च भगवान् सदा
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा स्तूयसे ऽच्युत किं मया ॥
202.m:
Always the pervader, the pervaded, the action, the agent, and the effect, O Blessed One,
the self of the self of all beings—how can you be praised by me, O Acyuta?

202.s:
paramātmā tvam ātmā ca bhūtātmā cāvyayo bhavān
yadā tadā stutir nāsti kimarthaṃ te pravartatām //
202.d:
परमात्मा त्वम् आत्मा च भूतात्मा चाव्ययो भवान्
यदा तदा स्तुतिर् नास्ति किमर्थं ते प्रवर्तताम् ॥
202.m:
When you are the supreme self, the self, the self of beings, and the imperishable one,
then praise does not exist; to what end should it proceed for you?

202.s:
prasīda sarvabhūtātman narakena kṛtaṃ ca yat
tat kṣamyatām adoṣāya matsutaḥ sa nipātitaḥ //
202.d:
प्रसीद सर्वभूतात्मन् नरकेन कृतं च यत्
तत् क्षम्यताम् अदोषाय मत्सुतः स निपातितः ॥
202.m:
Be gracious, O Self of all beings! And whatever was done by Naraka,
let that be forgiven; so that he would be guiltless, my son was struck down.

202.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tatheti coktvā dharaṇīṃ bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ
ratnāni narakāvāsāj jagrāha munisattamāḥ //
202.d:
व्यास उवाच
तथेति चोक्त्वा धरणीं भगवान् भूतभावनः
रत्नानि नरकावासाज् जग्राह मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
202.m:
Vyāsa said:
Saying "So be it" to the Earth, the Blessed One, creator of beings,
took the jewels from Naraka's dwelling, O best of sages.

202.s:
kanyāpure sa kanyānāṃ ṣoḍaśātulavikramaḥ
śatādhikāni dadṛśe sahasrāṇi dvijottamāḥ //
202.d:
कन्यापुरे स कन्यानां षोडशातुलविक्रमः
शताधिकानि ददृशे सहस्राणि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
202.m:
In the women's quarters he of peerless valor saw sixteen thousand
and one hundred maidens, O best of the twice-born.

202.s:
caturdaṃṣṭrān gajāṃś cogrān ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi dṛṣṭavān
kāmbojānāṃ tathāśvānāṃ niyutāny ekaviṃśatim //
202.d:
चतुर्दंष्ट्रान् गजांश् चोग्रान् षट् सहस्राणि दृष्टवान्
काम्बोजानां तथाश्वानां नियुतान्य् एकविंशतिम् ॥
202.m:
He also saw six thousand fierce elephants with four tusks,
and two million one hundred thousand Kāmboja horses.

202.s:
kanyās tāś ca tathā nāgāṃs tān aśvān dvārakāṃ purīm
prāpayām āsa govindaḥ sadyo narakakiṃkaraiḥ //
202.d:
कन्यास् ताश् च तथा नागांस् तान् अश्वान् द्वारकां पुरीम्
प्रापयाम् आस गोविन्दः सद्यो नरककिंकरैः ॥
202.m:
Those maidens, and likewise those elephants and horses,
Govinda dispatched immediately to the city of Dvārakā by Naraka's servants.

202.s:
dadṛśe vāruṇaṃ chattraṃ tathaiva maṇiparvatam
āropayām āsa harir garuḍe patageśvare //
202.d:
ददृशे वारुणं छत्त्रं तथैव मणिपर्वतम्
आरोपयाम् आस हरिर् गरुडे पतगेश्वरे ॥
202.m:
He saw the umbrella of Varuṇa and likewise the Jewel Mountain;
Hari loaded them onto Garuḍa, the lord of birds.

202.s:
āruhya ca svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ satyabhāmāsahāyavān
adityāḥ kuṇḍale dātuṃ jagāma tridaśālayam //
202.d:
आरुह्य च स्वयं कृष्णः सत्यभामासहायवान्
अदित्याः कुण्डले दातुं जगाम त्रिदशालयम् ॥
202.m:
Mounting [him] himself along with his companion Satyabhāmā,
Kṛṣṇa went to the abode of the gods to give the earrings to Aditi.

203.s:
vyāsa uvāca
garuḍo vāruṇaṃ chattraṃ tathaiva maṇiparvatam
sabhāryaṃ ca hṛṣīkeśaṃ līlayaiva vahan yayau //
203.d:
व्यास उवाच
गरुडो वारुणं छत्त्रं तथैव मणिपर्वतम्
सभार्यं च हृषीकेशं लीलयैव वहन् ययौ ॥
203.m:
Vyāsa said:
Effortlessly carrying the umbrella of Varuṇa, the Jewel Mountain,
and Hṛṣīkeśa accompanied by his wife, Garuḍa went forth.

203.s:
tataḥ śaṅkham upādhmāya svargadvāraṃ gato hariḥ
upatasthus tato devāḥ sārghapātrā janārdanam //
203.d:
ततः शङ्खम् उपाध्माय स्वर्गद्वारं गतो हरिः
उपतस्थुस् ततो देवाः सार्घपात्रा जनार्दनम् ॥
203.m:
Then Hari, having blown his conch, reached the gate of heaven;
there the gods, holding vessels of argha offerings, approached Janārdana.

203.s:
sa devair arcitaḥ kṛṣṇo devamātur niveśanam
sitābhraśikharākāraṃ praviśya dadṛśe 'ditim //
203.d:
स देवैर् अर्चितः कृष्णो देवमातुर् निवेशनम्
सिताभ्रशिखराकारं प्रविश्य ददृशे ऽदितिम् ॥
203.m:
Worshiped by the gods, Kṛṣṇa entered the dwelling of the mother of the gods,
which resembled the peak of a white cloud, and saw Aditi.

203.s:
sa tāṃ praṇamya śakreṇa sahitaḥ kuṇḍalottame
dadau narakanāśaṃ ca śaśaṃsāsyai janārdanaḥ //
203.d:
स तां प्रणम्य शक्रेण सहितः कुण्डलोत्तमे
ददौ नरकनाशं च शशंसास्यै जनार्दनः ॥
203.m:
Bowing to her together with Śakra, Janārdana gave her
the two excellent earrings and told her of the destruction of Naraka.

203.s:
tataḥ prītā jaganmātā dhātāraṃ jagatāṃ harim
tuṣṭāvāditir avyagraṃ kṛtvā tatpravaṇaṃ manaḥ //
203.d:
ततः प्रीता जगन्माता धातारं जगतां हरिम्
तुष्टावादितिर् अव्यग्रं कृत्वा तत्प्रवणं मनः ॥
203.m:
Then, delighted, Aditi, mother of the worlds, praised Hari,
the creator of the worlds, making her focused mind intent on him.

203.s:
aditir uvāca
namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa bhaktānām abhayaṃkara
sanātanātman bhūtātman sarvātman bhūtabhāvana //
203.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
नमस् ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष भक्तानाम् अभयंकर
सनातनात्मन् भूतात्मन् सर्वात्मन् भूतभावन ॥
203.m:
Aditi said:
Homage to you, lotus-eyed one, granter of fearlessness to devotees,
eternal self, self of beings, self of all, creator of beings!

203.s:
praṇetar manaso buddher indriyāṇāṃ guṇātmaka
sitadīrghādiniḥśeṣakalpanāparivarjita //
203.d:
प्रणेतर् मनसो बुद्धेर् इन्द्रियाणां गुणात्मक
सितदीर्घादिनिःशेषकल्पनापरिवर्जित ॥
203.m:
Guide of the mind, the intellect, and the senses, composed of the guṇas,
devoid of all conceptual constructs such as white or long!

203.s:
janmādibhir asaṃspṛṣṭasvapnādivārivarjitaḥ
saṃdhyā rātrir ahar bhūmir gaganaṃ vāyur ambu ca //
203.d:
जन्मादिभिर् असंस्पृष्टस्वप्नादिवारिवर्जितः
संध्या रात्रिर् अहर् भूमिर् गगनं वायुर् अम्बु च ॥
203.m:
Untouched by birth and the like, devoid of sleep and the like;
you are twilight, night, day, earth, sky, wind, and water,

203.s:
hutāśano mano buddhir bhūtādis tvaṃ tathācyuta
sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāṃ kartā kartṛpatir bhavān //
203.d:
हुताशनो मनो बुद्धिर् भूतादिस् त्वं तथाच्युत
सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशानां कर्ता कर्तृपतिर् भवान् ॥
203.m:
fire, mind, intellect, and the ego-principle, O Acyuta!
You are the agent of creation, preservation, and destruction, the lord of agents.

203.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivākhyābhir ātmamūrtibhir īśvaraḥ
māyābhir etad vyāptaṃ te jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam //
203.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाख्याभिर् आत्ममूर्तिभिर् ईश्वरः
मायाभिर् एतद् व्याप्तं ते जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
203.m:
Through your forms known as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, you are the Lord;
by your illusory powers this world, moving and unmoving, is pervaded.

203.s:
anātmany ātmavijñānaṃ sā te māyā janārdana
ahaṃ mameti bhāvo 'tra yayā samupajāyate //
203.d:
अनात्मन्य् आत्मविज्ञानं सा ते माया जनार्दन
अहं ममेति भावो ऽत्र यया समुपजायते ॥
203.m:
The notion of self in what is not-self is that illusory power of yours, O Janārdana,
by which the feeling of "I" and "mine" arises here.

203.s:
saṃsāramadhye māyāyās tavaitan nātha ceṣṭitam
yaiḥ svadharmaparair nātha narair ārādhito bhavān //
203.d:
संसारमध्ये मायायास् तवैतन् नाथ चेष्टितम्
यैः स्वधर्मपरैर् नाथ नरैर् आराधितो भवान् ॥
203.m:
In the midst of saṃsāra, O Lord, this is the working of your illusory power;
by those men devoted to their own dharma by whom you, O Lord, are worshiped,

203.s:
te taranty akhilām etāṃ māyām ātmavimuktaye
brahmādyāḥ sakalā devā manuṣyāḥ paśavas tathā //
203.d:
ते तरन्त्य् अखिलाम् एतां मायाम् आत्मविमुक्तये
ब्रह्माद्याः सकला देवा मनुष्याः पशवस् तथा ॥
203.m:
they cross over this entire illusory power for the sake of self-liberation.
All gods beginning with Brahmā, humans, and likewise beasts,

203.s:
viṣṇumāyāmahāvarte mohāndhatamasāvṛtāḥ
ārādhya tvām abhīpsante kāmān ātmabhavakṣaye //
203.d:
विष्णुमायामहावर्ते मोहान्धतमसावृताः
आराध्य त्वाम् अभीप्सन्ते कामान् आत्मभवक्षये ॥
203.m:
covered in blinding darkness of delusion within the great whirlpool of Viṣṇu's illusory power,
having worshiped you, desire sense-pleasures at the dissolution of their own existence.

203.s:
pade te puruṣā baddhā māyayā bhagavaṃs tava
mayā tvaṃ putrakāminyā vairipakṣakṣayāya ca //
203.d:
पदे ते पुरुषा बद्धा मायया भगवंस् तव
मया त्वं पुत्रकामिन्या वैरिपक्षक्षयाय च ॥
203.m:
Bound at your feet by illusory power, O Blessed One, are all men;
by me, desiring sons and the destruction of the enemy faction,

203.s:
ārādhito na mokṣāya māyāvilasitaṃ hi tat
kaupīnācchādanaprāyā vāñchā kalpadrumād api //
203.d:
आराधितो न मोक्षाय मायाविलसितं हि तत्
कौपीनाच्छादनप्राया वाञ्छा कल्पद्रुमाद् अपि ॥
203.m:
you were worshiped, but not for liberation; for that is the play of illusory power.
When even from the wish-fulfilling tree a desire arises

203.s:
jāyate yad apuṇyānāṃ so 'parādhaḥ svadoṣajaḥ
tat prasīdākhilajaganmāyāmohakarāvyaya //
203.d:
जायते यद् अपुण्यानां सो ऽपराधः स्वदोषजः
तत् प्रसीदाखिलजगन्मायामोहकराव्यय ॥
203.m:
merely for a loincloth on the part of the meritless, that offense is born of one's own fault.
Therefore be gracious, O imperishable creator of delusion through the illusory power of the entire world!

203.s:
ajñānaṃ jñānasadbhāva bhūtabhūteśa nāśaya
namas te cakrahastāya śārṅgahastāya te namaḥ //
203.d:
अज्ञानं ज्ञानसद्भाव भूतभूतेश नाशय
नमस् ते चक्रहस्ताय शार्ङ्गहस्ताय ते नमः ॥
203.m:
Destroy ignorance, O true essence of knowledge, lord of beings and elements!
Homage to you who hold the discus in hand; homage to you who hold the Śārṅga bow in hand!

203.s:
gadāhastāya te viṣṇo śaṅkhahastāya te namaḥ
etat paśyāmi te rūpaṃ sthūlacihnopaśobhitam
na jānāmi paraṃ yat te prasīda parameśvara //
203.d:
गदाहस्ताय ते विष्णो शङ्खहस्ताय ते नमः
एतत् पश्यामि ते रूपं स्थूलचिह्नोपशोभितम्
न जानामि परं यत् ते प्रसीद परमेश्वर ॥

203.s:
vyāsa uvāca
adityaivaṃ stuto viṣṇuḥ prahasyāha surāraṇim //
203.d:
व्यास उवाच
अदित्यैवं स्तुतो विष्णुः प्रहस्याह सुरारणिम् ॥
203.m:
Vyāsa said:
Thus praised by Aditi, Viṣṇu smiled and said to the mother of the gods:

203.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
mātā devi tvam asmākaṃ prasīda varadā bhava //
203.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
माता देवि त्वम् अस्माकं प्रसीद वरदा भव ॥
203.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O goddess, you are our mother; be gracious, be the granter of boons!

203.s:
aditir uvāca
evam astu yathecchā te tvam aśeṣasurāsuraiḥ
ajeyaḥ puruṣavyāghra martyaloke bhaviṣyasi //
203.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
एवम् अस्तु यथेच्छा ते त्वम् अशेषसुरासुरैः
अजेयः पुरुषव्याघ्र मर्त्यलोके भविष्यसि ॥
203.m:
Aditi said:
So be it, according to your wish! By all the gods and Asuras
you shall be unconquerable in the world of mortals, O tiger among men!

203.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tato 'nantaram evāsya śakrāṇīsahitāṃ ditim
satyabhāmā praṇamyāha prasīdeti punaḥ punaḥ //
203.d:
व्यास उवाच
ततो ऽनन्तरम् एवास्य शक्राणीसहितां दितिम्
सत्यभामा प्रणम्याह प्रसीदेति पुनः पुनः ॥
203.m:
Vyāsa said:
Immediately after this, Satyabhāmā bowed to Diti accompanied by Śakra's wife
and said repeatedly, "Be gracious!"

203.s:
aditir uvāca
matprasādān na te subhru jarā vairūpyam eva ca
bhaviṣyaty anavadyāṅgi sarvakāmā bhaviṣyasi //
203.d:
अदितिर् उवाच
मत्प्रसादान् न ते सुभ्रु जरा वैरूप्यम् एव च
भविष्यत्य् अनवद्याङ्गि सर्वकामा भविष्यसि ॥
203.m:
Aditi said:
By my grace, O fair-browed one, neither old age nor disfigurement
shall happen to you, O flawless-limbed one; you shall have all your desires fulfilled!

203.s:
vyāsa uvāca
adityā tu kṛtānujño devarājo janārdanam
yathāvat pūjayām āsa bahumānapuraḥsaram //
203.d:
व्यास उवाच
अदित्या तु कृतानुज्ञो देवराजो जनार्दनम्
यथावत् पूजयाम् आस बहुमानपुरःसरम् ॥
203.m:
Vyāsa said:
Permitted by Aditi, the king of the gods properly worshiped
Janārdana with great respect.

203.s:
tato dadarśa kṛṣṇo 'pi satyabhāmāsahāyavān
devodyānāni sarvāṇi nandanādīni sattamāḥ //
203.d:
ततो ददर्श कृष्णो ऽपि सत्यभामासहायवान्
देवोद्यानानि सर्वाणि नन्दनादीनि सत्तमाः ॥
203.m:
Then Kṛṣṇa too, accompanied by Satyabhāmā, saw
all the divine gardens, Nandana and the others, O best of men.

203.s:
dadarśa ca sugandhāḍhyaṃ mañjarīpuñjadhāriṇam
śaityāhlādakaraṃ divyaṃ tāmrapallavaśobhitam //
203.d:
ददर्श च सुगन्धाढ्यं मञ्जरीपुञ्जधारिणम्
शैत्याह्लादकरं दिव्यं ताम्रपल्लवशोभितम् ॥
203.m:
He also saw [the tree] rich in fragrance, bearing clusters of blossoms,
producing coolness and joy, divine, adorned with copper-colored sprouts,

203.s:
mathyamāne 'mṛte jātaṃ jātarūpasamaprabham
pārijātaṃ jagannāthaḥ keśavaḥ keśisūdanaḥ
taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha govindaṃ satyabhāmā dvijottamāḥ //
203.d:
मथ्यमाने ऽमृते जातं जातरूपसमप्रभम्
पारिजातं जगन्नाथः केशवः केशिसूदनः
तं दृष्ट्वा प्राह गोविन्दं सत्यभामा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
203.m:
the Pārijāta, born when the nectar was churned, resembling gold in splendor.
Seeing it, Keśava, slayer of Keśin, Lord of the World—
seeing it, Satyabhāmā spoke to Govinda, O best of the twice-born:

203.s:
satyabhāmovāca
kasmān na dvārakām eṣa nīyate kṛṣṇa pādapaḥ
yadi te tad vacaḥ satyaṃ satyātyarthaṃ priyeti me //
203.d:
सत्यभामोवाच
कस्मान् न द्वारकाम् एष नीयते कृष्ण पादपः
यदि ते तद् वचः सत्यं सत्यात्यर्थं प्रियेति मे ॥
203.m:
Satyabhāmā said:
Why is this tree not taken to Dvārakā, O Kṛṣṇa,
if that word of yours is true, that "Satyā is exceedingly dear to me"?

203.s:
madgṛhe niṣkuṭārthāya tad ayaṃ nīyatāṃ taruḥ
na me jāmbavatī tādṛg abhīṣṭā na ca rukmiṇī //
203.d:
मद्गृहे निष्कुटार्थाय तद् अयं नीयतां तरुः
न मे जाम्बवती तादृग् अभीष्टा न च रुक्मिणी ॥
